cases.case_summary: A newborn was referred at 5 days of life with axial hypotonia, poor head control, poor sucking, and a peculiar senile appearance.
cases.full_text:
A newborn was referred at 5 days of life with axial hypotonia, poor head control, poor sucking, and a peculiar senile appearance.
Birth history: Male third-born infant of non-consanguineous parents with an unremarkable family history and healthy siblings, born vaginally at 38 weeks + 1 day after a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy.
Apgar scores and birth measurements: Apgar scores 9 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, attributed to persistent hypotonia. Weight 2560 g (10th percentile), length 49 cm (25th–50th percentile), head circumference 35 cm (50th–75th percentile).
First neonatal examination: Axial hypotonia, joint hypermobility, right congenital genu recurvatum that resolved within 12 hours, arachnodactyly, and finger joint contractures. Hearing, pulse-oximetry, and inborn-error-of-metabolism screens were normal.
Facial examination: Hypertelorism, down-slanting palpebral fissures, ocular exotropia, arched nose with a bulbous nasal tip, high-vaulted palate, short philtrum, down-turned mouth with a thin upper lip, micrognathia, and low-set ears with evident lobes. No cleft palate.
Skin and limb examination: Lax, translucent skin; arachnodactyly; contracted finger joints; adduction deformity of the right thumb; clinodactyly and ulnar deviation of all fingers; camptodactyly of the feet with a tendency of the toes to flex; dystrophic nails. No pterygia.
Echocardiography: Aortic root at the sinus measured 13 mm (Z score +3) without aortic insufficiency; the remaining aortic segments were within limits. Patent foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus with a hemodynamically nonsignificant left-to-right shunt.
Ophthalmic examination and abdominal ultrasound: Exotropia was confirmed, with no other ocular abnormalities. Abdominal ultrasound showed no abnormalities.
Trio whole-exome sequencing: Novel heterozygous de novo missense variant c.1378C>G, p.(Arg460Gly) in TGFBR2 (NM_003242.5).

cases.case_summary: A 35-year-old man presented to the emergency department with numbness and lower-limb heaviness for 1 month. The symptoms had progressed gradually until he could no longer walk, and he had difficulty passing urine and fecal incontinence.
cases.full_text:
A 35-year-old man presented to the emergency department with numbness and lower-limb heaviness for 1 month. The symptoms had progressed gradually until he could no longer walk, and he had difficulty passing urine and fecal incontinence.
Lower-limb motor examination: Paraplegia with muscle power 2/5
Limb neurological examination: Upper-limb bulk, power, and reflexes normal; lower-limb deep tendon reflexes absent, Babinski responses positive, walking impossible, and no sensory disorder
Spinal MRI: Extradural spinal lesion at T7-T10, about 8.0 cm × 1.2 cm, located at the dorsal spinal cord
MRI signal: Hyperintense on T1- and T2-weighted images and heterogeneous on STIR
Contrast-enhanced MRI: Maximal enhancement after intravenous contrast, with compression of the spinal cord
Intraoperative inspection: Epidural lesion about 8 cm × 1.8 cm, red, tough, with regular margins and a very rich blood supply
Histopathology: Lesion made up of fatty tissue and angioma-like tissue

cases.case_summary: A 47-year-old man is referred with a 2-month history of jaundice, weight loss, and intermittent low fever.
cases.full_text:
A 47-year-old man is referred with a 2-month history of jaundice, weight loss, and intermittent low fever.
Abdominal examination: Tender mass in the right upper quadrant
Computed tomography of the liver: 9.0 cm mass in segments VI and VII with contrast enhancement in the arterial phase and washout at the equilibrium phase
Colonoscopy and upper endoscopy: Normal
Hepatitis B and C serology: Negative
Serum alpha-fetoprotein: 2.3 ng/dL
Leukocyte count: 12,800 cell/mm3
C-reactive protein: 5.2 mg/dL
Percutaneous liver biopsy: Hepatic tissue with proliferation of spindle-shaped cells mixed with inflammatory myofibrohistiocytes

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old man presented with persistent right upper abdominal pain for 6 months that was relieved by medication but then recurred. After 4 months, he noticed progressive jaundice, clay-colored stools, itching, significant weight loss, and anorexia.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old man presented with persistent right upper abdominal pain for 6 months that was relieved by medication but then recurred. After 4 months, he noticed progressive jaundice, clay-colored stools, itching, significant weight loss, and anorexia.
Right upper abdominal pain: Persistent pain in the right upper abdomen for 6 months, relieved with medication, which then recurred.
Jaundice and associated symptoms: After 4 months, progressive jaundice, clay-colored stools, itching, significant weight loss, and anorexia.
Physical examination: Icteric, with no lymphadenopathy. The gallbladder was palpable, smooth, and firm.
Serum bilirubin and liver enzymes: Total bilirubin 6.93 mg/dL with direct component 4.26 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase 175 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 153 U/L, and alkaline phosphate 1100 U/L.
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the gallbladder and bile duct: Enhancing thickening at the gallbladder neck up to 5.5 mm, with periductal spread along the cystic duct and proximal common bile duct causing obstruction and proximal intrahepatic biliary radical dilatation.
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of regional lymph nodes: Multiple homogeneously enhancing discrete lymph nodes in the periportal, precaval, and interaortocaval regions, without compression of the biliary system.
Histopathology of the gallbladder, lymph nodes, and bile-duct margin: Extensive caseous necrosis and numerous epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells in the gallbladder; lymph nodes and the common bile duct resection margin showed similar features.
Ziehl-Neelsen stain of the gallbladder: Acid-fast bacilli were present.

cases.case_summary: In May 2020, a 45-year-old woman presents with four years of severe generalized itching and skin lesions and with one month of gradual vision loss in both eyes, recurrent fever, and weight loss.
cases.full_text:
In May 2020, a 45-year-old woman presents with four years of severe generalized itching and skin lesions and with one month of gradual vision loss in both eyes, recurrent fever, and weight loss.
Exposure and family history: Husband has a similar skin lesion for a long time and has lived in South Africa for the last 8 years. Other family members are well, with no similar lesions. She denied tuberculosis or contact with smear-positive tuberculosis and had not received a blood transfusion.
General examination: Emaciated and moderately anaemic, with normal vital signs and no lymphadenopathy.
Skin and mucosal examination: Multiple excoriated lichenified papules on the extremities, neck, and upper back, with exudation and crusting of some lesions; whitish patches on the tongue and oral cavity; and a nonhealing ulcer on the labia.
Fundoscopy: Right eye with disc swelling, haemorrhage, and exudate in the superior and inferior quadrants; left eye with a pale disc and exudates in the superior and inferior retinal quadrants.
HIV ELISA: Positive.
Syphilis, viral hepatitis, and HSV serology: Serum VDRL, TPHA, HBsAg, HCV antibody, and HSV-1 and HSV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies were negative.
CD4 count: 237 cells/mm.

cases.case_summary: A 77-year-old woman presented with intermittent hoarse voice and episodes of choking when swallowing.
cases.full_text:
A 77-year-old woman presented with intermittent hoarse voice and episodes of choking when swallowing.
Voice: Intermittent hoarse voice
Swallowing: Episodes of choking when swallowing
Panendoscopy: Smooth, cystic mass arising from the right posterior aryepiglottic fold
Mucosal biopsy: Mild mucosal dysplasia only
Ultrasound-guided biopsy: Spindle cells
Contrast CT of the neck: At C5/6, an enhancing right thyroid lobe and a non-enhancing mass with a clearly visible plane of separation between them
FISH: Signal pattern consistent with SS-18 gene rearrangement

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old man was referred with a 3-month history of dyspnoea, hacking cough, and distended jugular veins.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old man was referred with a 3-month history of dyspnoea, hacking cough, and distended jugular veins.
Earlier blood count, bone marrow biopsy, and JAK2 testing: Seven years earlier, a blood count showed polyglobulia. Bone marrow cellularity was 70%, with trilinear expansion, a myelo-erythroid ratio of 5:1, and preserved maturation; megakaryocytes were slightly polymorphic with little clustering. The marrow was considered highly suspicious for an initial phase of polycythemia vera, and he was then treated with oral 1,4-bis (3-bromopropionyl) piperazine 25 mg and hydroxyurea 500 mg. Three years later, JAK2 V617F was found.
Physical examination: Facial rash, periorbital and facial edema, distended jugular veins, bilateral disappearance of the supraclavicular fossae, mild ptosis especially on the right, and a hard chest-wall mass over the sixth right rib.
Blood tests: Lymphocytes 17.5% and 1.57×10^3/μL; LDH 423 U/L; CRP 1.8 mg/dL; fibrinogen 414 mg/dL; IgA 549 mg/dL; ESR 27 mm; β2-microglobulin 2.6 mg/dL.
Viral testing: Negative for HCV, HHV8, and HIV. Positive for HBV, with HBc IgG 627 mIU/mL, and positive for EBV.
Total-body computed tomography: A few days after admission, a polylobed solid anterior-superior mediastinal lesion was iso-hypodense after contrast and measured 9.7 cm transversely, 8 cm craniocaudally, and 5.7 cm anteroposteriorly. It compressed the right jugular vein and the superior vena cava. The chest-wall lesion had the same radiologic characteristics. No lesion was seen in the abdomen or skull.
Histologic examination: The mediastinal fine-needle aspirate and the chest-wall biopsy showed the same findings: tissue widely occupied by a monomorphic lymphoid proliferation of large cells with evident nucleoli.
Immunophenotyping: LCA positive and CD20 negative; CD79a, MUM1, CD38, and CD138 positive; kappa positive and lambda negative; CD56, CD30, ALK1, CD3, CD5, CD10, bcl-2, bcl-6, TdT, and LMP1 negative; Ki-67 85%.
Additional immunohistochemical stains: Pan-cytokeratin, CK20, chromogranin, and NSE were negative.

cases.case_summary: A 48-year-old woman presented with progressive, painless decreased vision in the left eye for 2 months.
cases.full_text:
A 48-year-old woman presented with progressive, painless decreased vision in the left eye for 2 months.
Visual acuity: Light perception in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye.
Biomicroscopy of the left eye: No conjunctival hyperemia, a clear cornea, and no inflammation in the anterior chamber.
Fundus examination and fluorescein angiography of the left eye: Retinal detachment with a large superior brownish mass.
B-scan ultrasonography of the left eye: Large choroidal dome-shaped mass surrounded by subretinal fluid, with neither acoustic hollowing nor calcification.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the orbits: Intraocular tumor measuring 12 × 11 × 11 mm, with high signal intensity on T1-weighted images, low signal intensity on T2, collar-button extension, and enhancement on T1-weighted images after gadolinium.
Extraocular extension on orbital imaging: Scleral thickening and no evidence of extraocular tumor extension.
Histopathology of the enucleated eye: Brownish-black pigmented tumor arising from the choroid, composed of fusiform cells with brownish cytoplasm, elongated nuclei, and small nucleoli, with no signs of necrosis or malignancy.
Immunohistochemistry: Positive cytoplasmic reaction for S-100 protein and HMB-45 monoclonal antibody.

cases.case_summary: A 70-year-old man presents with an unpleasant burning sensation of the distal upper and lower extremities and scalp for 3 months.
cases.full_text:
A 70-year-old man presents with an unpleasant burning sensation of the distal upper and lower extremities and scalp for 3 months.
Respiratory and limb symptom history: Shortness of breath of subacute onset for 4 years and nonprogressive bilateral lower limb swelling for 6 months.
Chest CT: Reticular nodular opacities in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe, superior segment of the right lower lobe, and left superior lingular lobe; thickening of the right horizontal fissure; no lung masses or cavitary lesions; pretracheal, right paratracheal, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, largest 2 cm at the right hilum.
Contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys: Diffuse ill-defined hypodense lesions in both kidneys without arterial-phase enhancement: left mid-pole lesion 3 cm × 4 cm × 5 cm and right lower-pole lesion 3.5 cm × 3.5 cm × 4 cm.
Renal biopsy histology: Dense lymphoplasmocytic infiltration and storiform fibrosis with tubulointerstitial nephritis; no granulomata.
Neurological examination: Right-sided hemisensory loss, described as a residual deficit from a previous stroke, and no objective evidence of peripheral neuropathy.
Nerve conduction studies: Mononeuritis multiplex.
IgG4 immunostaining of the renal biopsy: More than 25 cells per high-power field.
Serum complement: C3 77 mg/dL (reference 83–177 mg/dL) and C4 9 mg/dL (reference 12–36 mg/dL).

cases.case_summary: A 37-year-old woman has had right facial pain for 4 months and progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe for 3 months.
cases.full_text:
A 37-year-old woman has had right facial pain for 4 months and progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe for 3 months.
Examination of the auricular swelling: Soft swelling in the anteroinferior auricular area; the mass was smooth, elastic, mobile, painful on pressure, and not fluctuant.
Facial nerve examination: Facial nerve function was normal.
Cervical lymph node examination: No cervical lymph node was palpable.
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography: Well-defined soft tissue mass, 40 mm × 25 mm, in the right deep parotid lobe.
Gross examination of the excised mass: Grayish-red collagenous mass intermingled with myxoid.
Microscopic examination: Hypocellular to moderately cellular myxoid or fibromyxoid areas, curvilinear capillaries with perivascular cell condensation, and fusiform cells ranging from small and bland to enlarged, bizarre, pleomorphic, and multinucleated, with scant slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm and infrequent mitoses.
Histologic architecture: Myxoid areas with spindle cells in a pleomorphic storiform pattern.
Immunohistochemical staining: Tumor cells strongly immunoreactive for vimentin and alpha1-antichymotrypsin; Ki-67 labeling index 35%; assays for desmin, alpha-smooth muscle actin, beta2-microglobulin, and CD34 were negative.
cases.final_diagnosis: parotid myxofibrosarcoma of low histological grade

cases.case_summary: A 59-year-old woman presented with visual disturbances of her left eye and hyperemia of both eyes. She was generally in good health and had a painless moon face.
cases.full_text:
A 59-year-old woman presented with visual disturbances of her left eye and hyperemia of both eyes. She was generally in good health and had a painless moon face.
Earlier evaluation of facial swelling: Facial swelling had been noted 1 year earlier. A general systemic examination detected no abnormal findings.
Evaluation of neck stiffness: Stiffness of the right side of the neck developed 3 months earlier. Echography and computed tomography showed bilateral enlargement of the lacrimal glands and extraocular muscles and enlargement of the right parotid gland. Two right parotid biopsies were within normal limits.
Ophthalmic examination: Visual acuity was 20/25 in each eye, and Hertel exophthalmometry was 15 mm in each eye. The left eye had blepharoptosis and hypertropia. Upward gaze was limited in the right eye, and downward and rightward gaze were limited in the left eye. She had no diplopia or eye pain. Slit-lamp examination showed only chemosis and hyperemia of both eyes, and the fundi were normal.
Contrast magnetic resonance imaging: Discrete spindle-shaped enlargement of the bellies of all extraocular muscles in both eyes, without spillover into the orbital fat. The lacrimal and parotid glands were enlarged, and the subcutaneous tissue of the face was hyperplastic.
Peripheral blood tests: WBC, CRP, serum IL-2, IgG4, and thyroid-related hormones were within normal limits. LDH and ferritin were slightly higher than the standard level. Tests for adult T-cell leukemia and HIV antibodies were negative, and tests for Epstein-Barr virus were positive.
Gallium scintigraphy, flow cytometry, bone marrow aspirate and trephine, and lumbar puncture: No abnormal findings were detected.
Biopsy of the left inferior rectus and right parotid gland: Atypical cells infiltrated the tissues. The cells were positive for CD3, CD5, CD8, and Granzyme B and negative for CD20, CD56, and CD79a.

cases.case_summary: A 17-year-old girl presents with a progressively increasing swelling over the right frontoparietal region for 6 months and headache localized to the swelling.
cases.full_text:
A 17-year-old girl presents with a progressively increasing swelling over the right frontoparietal region for 6 months and headache localized to the swelling.
Prior head injury: A fall 1 year and 6 months earlier caused scalp swelling, a bruise, and a depressed skull fracture in the right frontal area at the same site, managed conservatively.
Scalp and skull examination: Fluctuant right frontoparietal swelling measuring 10 × 7 cm with a palpable bone defect; tender, without signs of inflammation or skin color change; multiple palpable bone defects in the right frontal area.
General physical and routine hematologic examination: No abnormality on general physical examination or routine hematologic testing.
Head CT: Extensive bony defect involving both the inner and outer tables, with a slightly hyperdense epidural and subgaleal lesion containing mixed hypodense areas and adjacent brain parenchymal hypodensity.
Brain MRI: Epidural and subgaleal lesion iso- to hyperintense on T1 and T2 with intervening hypointense areas, T2 hyperintensity in the adjacent brain, mass effect on the brain and lateral ventricle with midline shift, and homogeneous enhancement with non-enhancing hypodense areas.
Operative inspection of the collection: Thin, non-offensive whitish material in the subgaleal and epidural spaces, and a soft whitish cheesy epidural collection with a lesion adherent to the dura.
Inspection for subdural extension: No extension of the lesion into the subdural space.
Bone histopathology: Bony tissue fragments with extensive well-formed epithelioid granulomas and central areas of necrosis.

cases.case_summary: A 51-year-old woman presented to the emergency room in early May 2016 with repeated unconsciousness over 10 days. Her daily stool output had risen to 1.5–2 L, and her urine output had decreased since April.
cases.full_text:
A 51-year-old woman presented to the emergency room in early May 2016 with repeated unconsciousness over 10 days. Her daily stool output had risen to 1.5–2 L, and her urine output had decreased since April.
Prior surgery: Subtotal colectomy and ileostomy in February 2015
Resection specimen pathology: Diffuse pan-colitis consistent with UC and no indications of Crohn’s disease
Medication review: Not taking any medications, including NSAIDs
Ileostomy stool studies: Many leukocytes; repeated stool cultures and Clostridium difficile toxin tests negative
CMV and EBV testing: CMV-DNA, CMV-pp65, and EBV-DNA all negative
Pouchoscopy: Oedematous inflamed mucosa with patchy superficial ulcers in the diverted pouch
Upper endoscopy and endoscopy through the stoma: Normal gross appearance of the stomach, duodenum, and pre-stomal ileum
Duodenal and pre-stomal ileal biopsies: Moderate villous atrophy, cryptitis, decreased goblet cells, and severe active inflammation with neutrophil infiltration in the lamina propria, without intraepithelial lymphocytosis

cases.case_summary: A 46-year-old man was referred to clinic complaining of neck pain for 8 months.
cases.full_text:
A 46-year-old man was referred to clinic complaining of neck pain for 8 months.
Serum calcium: 12.5 mg/dl (normal range 8.7–10.7 mg/dl)
Serum phosphate: 1.5 mg/dl (normal range 2.5–5 mg/dl)
Serum parathyroid hormone: 1285 pg/ml (normal range 14.5–87.1 pg/ml)
Serum alkaline phosphatase: 875 U/L (normal range 80–360 U/L)
Neck ultrasound: Lesion in favor of parathyroid adenoma at the lower pole of the left parathyroid lobe
Cervical CT: Lytic lesion in C5 eroding the vertebral body, left pedicle, and lamina
Cervical MRI: C5 lesion with low signal on T1 and high signal on T2
Lesion biopsy: Scattered giant cell, peritrabecular fibrosis, and hemosiderin deposits

cases.case_summary: A 43-year-old woman was admitted with a 3-month history of flank pain, intermittent gross hematuria, weakness, and weight loss.
cases.full_text:
A 43-year-old woman was admitted with a 3-month history of flank pain, intermittent gross hematuria, weakness, and weight loss.
Bone and neurologic symptoms: No bone pain or neurologic symptoms
Urine examination: Microscopic hematuria
Blood biochemistry: Normal, including alkaline phosphatase and liver function tests
Abdominal CT: Large hypodense mass, maximum diameter 15 cm, in the left retroperitoneal space originating from the kidney, with irregular foci of calcification
Chest X-ray: No pathologic lesion
Macroscopic examination: 15 × 10 × 8.5 cm renal tumor with a central yellow-brown hard mass, cystic change, hemorrhage, necrosis, and prominent calcified whitish stone-like areas, grossly invading the renal sinus, pelvis, and renal sinus fat
Microscopic examination: Highly cellular tumor with spindle cell proliferation and interspersed unmineralized neoplastic osteoid, a high atypical malignant cartilage component, variably pleomorphic tumor cells with lace-like to compact trabeculae, epithelioid features, moderate atypia, and a few mitotic figures
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for vimentin and CD10; negative for Pan CK

cases.case_summary: A 10-year-old boy presented with persistent jaundice, intermittent itching, and clay-colored stool from 10 days after birth.
cases.full_text:
A 10-year-old boy presented with persistent jaundice, intermittent itching, and clay-colored stool from 10 days after birth.
Anthropometric measurements: Height 113 cm (z-score < −3), weight 13 kg (z-score < −3), body mass index 10.23 kg/m2, and mid-arm circumference 9 cm.
Facial examination: Triangular face with a broad forehead, deeply set eyes, hypertelorism, prominent ears, a small pointed chin, and a saddle nose with a bulbous tip.
Abdominal examination: The left hepatic lobe was enlarged. The liver was firm, with an irregular margin and a slightly nodular surface; liver span was 9 cm along the right mid-clavicular line. The spleen was firm and palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin.
Eye examination: Posterior embryotoxon, iris strands, and increased intraocular pressure.
Serum liver biochemical tests: Total bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL (reference 0.1–1.2 mg/dL), direct bilirubin 3.4 mg/dL (reference 0.1–0.3 mg/dL), AST 292 IU/L (reference 10–40 IU/L), ALT 121 IU/L (reference 10–50 IU/L), ALP 978 IU/L (reference 250–750 IU/L), GGT 24 IU/L (reference 0–30 IU/L), total protein 5.8 g/dL (reference 5.5–7.5 g/dL), and albumin 2.4 g/dL (reference 3.5–5.5 g/dL).
Hepatitis B and C serology: Hepatitis B surface antigen negative and anti-hepatitis C virus antibodies negative.
Echocardiography: Pulmonary hypertension and tricuspid regurgitation.
Liver biopsy: Ten portal tracts with conspicuous absence of interlobular bile ducts adjacent to hepatocytes, mild portal inflammation, some fibrosis, occasional nodules, and a few feathery hepatocytes without inflammation.

cases.case_summary: A 68-year-old left-hand-dominant man presents with numbness of the left thumb and a palpable mass along the flexor surface of the thumb.
cases.full_text:
A 68-year-old left-hand-dominant man presents with numbness of the left thumb and a palpable mass along the flexor surface of the thumb.
Hand tingling: Tingling in the left hand, mainly at night, for the last 3 years, with difficulty performing simple daily tasks because of thumb numbness.
Thumb mass: The mass had been present for 2 months and was tender to palpation.
Bowling history and grip: He had been an avid bowler in the past and reported a weakened grip while bowling since the symptoms began.
Prior hand trauma or nerve compression: He denied any history of hand trauma or previously diagnosed pathologic nerve compression.
Tinel sign and carpal compression test: Tinel sign was positive over the left thumb mass and at the carpal tunnel bilaterally, and the carpal compression test was positive on the left.
Static two-point discrimination: At least 5 mm at all digits, and greater than 15 mm at the ulnar digital nerve of the left thumb.
Electrodiagnostic testing: No compressive neuropathy and no cervical radiculopathy.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left hand: No definite abnormal signal or lesion in the region corresponding to the palpable mass.

cases.case_summary: A 32-year-old Asian woman presents for evaluation of an abnormal chest radiograph. She has no symptoms. A well-defined mass around the apex of the heart has enlarged over the past year.
cases.full_text:
A 32-year-old Asian woman presents for evaluation of an abnormal chest radiograph. She has no symptoms. A well-defined mass around the apex of the heart has enlarged over the past year.
Chest radiography: On radiographs from 2018 and 2019, the largest diameter of the mass increased from 34 mm to 64 mm.
Past medical, family, and exposure history: Never smoked. Hyperthyroidism had been treated with thiamazole, and she was medication-free on admission. No history of pregnancy or childbirth. No remarkable family history of illness, including cancer. Desk worker with no history of exposure to certain chemicals or asbestos.
Chest computed tomography: Pear-shaped mass, 80 mm in largest diameter, between the pericardium and the left lung; monotonous, with attenuation 23–32 HU; expansive growth without apparent invasion of adjacent organs.
Magnetic resonance imaging: Low signal on T1-weighted images and low, heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted fat-saturation images.
Magnetic resonance imaging for intratumoral fat: No fat intensity was detected inside the tumor.
Histologic examination: Paucicellular tumor composed of vaguely arranged bundles of wavy collagen fibers, with sparse cellularity and no apparent cytologic atypia. Nonspecific lymphocyte or mononuclear-cell infiltration of varying intensity was present around tumor vessels. The pedicle consisted of longitudinally arranged fibrous bundles connected to the pericardium.
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for alpha-smooth muscle actin, desmin, and CD34, with intact INI1. Negative for cytokeratin AE1/AE3, EMA, beta-catenin, S100 protein, D2-40, MDM2, and STAT6. No infiltration by IgG4-positive plasma cells.
Ki-67 index and ALK studies: Ki-67 labeling index less than 5%. ALK immunohistochemistry was negative, and fluorescence in situ hybridization showed no ALK gene breakage.

cases.case_summary: A 50-year-old woman was referred after 8 months with a palpable left thigh mass that had gradually enlarged and was painful.
cases.full_text:
A 50-year-old woman was referred after 8 months with a palpable left thigh mass that had gradually enlarged and was painful.
Past medical history: Hepatitis C virus carrier, with no other major preexisting medical conditions
Magnetic resonance imaging: Tumor in the left thigh with high signal intensity on T2-weighted images
Computed tomography: Liver mass measuring 140 mm × 80 mm × 120 mm
Chest computed tomography: No lesions in the lungs or pleura
Left thigh mass size and skin: 113 × 91 × 94 mm and nearly ulcerated on the skin
Gross examination of the excised mass: Well-defined 15 × 12 × 10 cm mass in the subcutaneous fatty tissue
Histological examination: Dense proliferation of variably sized round to short spindle-shaped cells, often with fatty droplets; some cells with adipoblast-like morphology; large nuclei and multinucleated cells, with prominent fission patterns and coagulative necrotic nests
Immunohistochemical staining: Only a few tumor cells positive for S-100 protein; the majority negative for cyclin-dependent kinase 4, murine double minute type 2, desmin, smooth muscle actin, cluster of differentiation 34, epithelial membrane antigen, and cytokeratin AE1/AE3

cases.case_summary: A 36-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of generalized epileptic activity and altered perception.
cases.full_text:
A 36-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of generalized epileptic activity and altered perception.
Past medical history: Unyielding
Neurological examination: Bilateral Babinski's sign
Cranial magnetic resonance imaging: Multiple dural-based enhancing lesions with cerebral edema
T1- and T2-weighted cranial MRI: Lesions iso- and hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Chest radiography: Appeared normal
Cerebrospinal fluid appearance: Clear
Dura at craniotomy: Outer layer firm, thickened, and avascular pinkish, firmly involving the inner layer as fibrous masses
Histological examination: Multiple confluent necrotizing and nonnecrotizing granulomas with multinucleated and Langhans-type giant cells

cases.case_summary: A patient presented with an 11-week history of sudden-onset painful swelling of the right upper arm.
cases.full_text:
A patient presented with an 11-week history of sudden-onset painful swelling of the right upper arm.
Prostate cancer history: T3bN0M0 Gleason score 4 + 5 prostatic adenocarcinoma, diagnosed 6 months before presentation
Medication history: LHRH injections started 3 months before presentation; current treatment leuprorelin acetate (Prostap) 11.25 mg once every 3 months
Right arm examination: Approximately 5 cm hard mass in the distal right biceps, just above the tendon
MRI of the right upper arm: Maximally 5.4 cm ill-defined heterogeneous mass in the distal right biceps muscle, just proximal to the tendon, with peripheral enhancement and slightly increased T2/T1 signal relative to skeletal muscle
Needle core biopsy histology: Fibrous tissue and skeletal muscle with extensive florid destructive granulomatous inflammation; ill-defined granulomas containing sheets of epithelioid histiocytes and giant cells, including foreign body type; histiocytes with plump ovoid vesicular nuclei without atypia; no caseation or necrosis
Histologic examination for foreign material: No foreign material identified; prominent rounded clear fatty vacuoles within the histiocytes
Immunohistochemistry: No neoplasm identified with desmin, smooth muscle actin, S100 protein, AE1/AE3, CD117, or CD34
Histochemical stains for microorganisms: No microorganisms identified with Ziehl-Neelsen, periodic acid-Schiff, or Grocott stains

cases.case_summary: A 45-year-old woman is admitted with palpitations for 14 years that have become more frequent and intense over the past two months, together with dyspnea on exertion and weight loss of two pounds per month.
cases.full_text:
A 45-year-old woman is admitted with palpitations for 14 years that have become more frequent and intense over the past two months, together with dyspnea on exertion and weight loss of two pounds per month.
History of palpitations: Palpitations for 14 years
Recent symptom course: Palpitations more frequent and intense in the last two months before admission, with dyspnea on exertion and weight loss of two pounds per month
Cardiovascular and general examination: Regular heart rhythm, splitting of S1, and no murmurs; examination of other systems normal
Electrocardiogram: Sinus rhythm with right bundle branch block and anterosuperior divisional block
Transthoracic echocardiography: Moving mass in the right atrium attached to the atrial septum, enlarged right atrium, right ventricular volume overload, and a dilated inferior vena cava
Chest computed tomography with intravenous contrast: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with an intra-atrial hypodensity measuring approximately 6.1 × 5.6 cm; the right atrium did not fill with contrast medium
Appearance of the excised mass: Mobile, pedunculated, lobulated, clear, and gelatinous, implanted at the atrial superior vena cava junction
Microscopy of the excised mass: Abundant myxoid stroma with stellate cells; necrosis, mitotic activity, atypia, and pleomorphism were not detected

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with a painful mass that had been growing on the left side of her neck for three months.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old woman presented with a painful mass that had been growing on the left side of her neck for three months.
Neck symptom history: Painful mass growing on the left lateral neck for three months
Constitutional symptoms: No fever and no weight loss
Neck examination: Hard, painful, fluctuant 10 × 7 cm mass in the supraclavicular region of the lateral neck, inflammatory overlying skin, and no regional lymphadenopathy
Blood count and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: Normal blood cell count with ESR 40 mm/h
Chest radiograph: No abnormality
Neck CT: Binocular left supraclavicular mass with a cystic aspect, measuring 14 × 10 cm and containing numerous thin-outlined cystic formations
Operative inspection: Cyst wall and daughter cysts visualized
Histopathology of the excised specimen: Inflammatory tissue surrounding a parasite-like cyst, with scoleces in the specimen

cases.case_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with a 2-year enlargement of the left mandible, with mild pain, swelling, and induration, and delayed eruption of the posterior molar on the same side.
cases.full_text:
A 13-year-old boy presented with a 2-year enlargement of the left mandible, with mild pain, swelling, and induration, and delayed eruption of the posterior molar on the same side.
Sensory complaint: Paresthesia, present from the onset.
Submandibular lymph node examination: Bilateral, mobile submandibular adenopathies, each less than 1 cm.
Intraoral examination: Cortical expansion in the left retromolar area, slight pain on palpation of the lingual plate, and stony consistency beneath healthy mucosa.
Panoramic radiograph: Large radiolucent area divided by thick radiopaque lines from the left mandibular parasymphysis to the condylar neck and coronoid process; tooth 38 displaced into the coronoid area.
Facial CT: Bone lesion centered in the left hemimandible, involving the condylar neck, ramus, angle, and hemibody, with cortical thinning.
Fine-needle aspiration: Aspiration of 3 cc of citrine fluid, followed by hematic fluid.
Histopathologic examination: Proliferation of epithelial cells with large clear cytoplasm, eosinophilic cytoplasm, and a squamous appearance, without differentiation to odontogenic tissue.
Periodic acid-Schiff stain: Positive for mucin.

cases.case_summary: A 36-year-old woman in her third pregnancy was referred at 13 weeks of gestation for first-trimester screening.
cases.full_text:
A 36-year-old woman in her third pregnancy was referred at 13 weeks of gestation for first-trimester screening.
Pregnancy history: 36-year-old woman in her third pregnancy, referred for first-trimester screening at 13 weeks of gestation
First-trimester fetal ultrasound: Fetal anatomy was regular except for an umbilical cord cyst
Umbilical cord cyst measurements: Maximum size 18 mm, regular margins, adjacent to the abdominal wall
Cyst vascularity and internal structure: Avascular, with no internal septa or vegetations
Cyst relation to cord vessels and bladder: Within the umbilical cord, embraced by the two umbilical arteries, and in communication with the bladder
Cyst size during the examination: Size varied during an ultrasound examination lasting several hours

cases.case_summary: A 27-year-old man was admitted in April 2018 after an episode in January 2018 of lip and facial swelling, generalized hives, and weakness.
cases.full_text:
A 27-year-old man was admitted in April 2018 after an episode in January 2018 of lip and facial swelling, generalized hives, and weakness.
Circumstances of the January episode: Symptoms began in January 2018 after gym exercise (isometric training, then treadmill), when he ate 2 kiwi fruits (Actinidia deliciosa). Lip swelling started within 5 minutes, followed by an itchy scalp and facial swelling. About 60 minutes later he developed generalized hives, weakness, and a rumbling sensation in the ears. Symptoms improved within 25 minutes after antihistamines, but facial swelling lasted 24 hours.
Earlier kiwi ingestion: He had previously eaten kiwi without any symptoms.
Other possible contributors on the day of the reaction: He denied excessive stress, alcohol, and NSAID use as factors that could have worsened the reaction. He ate breakfast that day but could not recall the foods.
Prick-by-prick test with fresh kiwi: Positive.
Skin prick tests with foods: Negative for rye flour, wheat flour, barley flour, orange, clementine, banana, potato, pepper, cod, carp, chicken egg, cow's milk, pork, beef, and meat II.
Exercise provocation while fasting: After a 10-minute bicycle warm-up reaching a heart rate of 120 bpm at 4 minutes, he exercised on a treadmill for 10 minutes at 80%–90% of maximum heart rate. He had no side effects during or after exercise.
Kiwi ingestion without exercise: He ate 2 ripe, peeled kiwi fruits in incremental doses and had no adverse effects over 24 hours of observation.
Kiwi ingestion followed by exercise: He ate one kiwi fruit, was observed for 30 minutes, then exercised. Five minutes after exercise he developed abdominal pain, urticarial lesions on the face, and a dry cough. Examination showed single wheezing over the lung fields, heart rate 80 bpm, and blood pressure 117/82 mmHg.

cases.case_summary: A five-year-old child presented to their cardiologist at an outside institution for routine follow-up and was in their usual state of health, with no chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, fatigue, or syncope.
cases.full_text:
A five-year-old child presented to their cardiologist at an outside institution for routine follow-up and was in their usual state of health, with no chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, fatigue, or syncope.
Past cardiac history: Known bicuspid aortic valve, mild aortic valve stenosis, and mild enlargement of the aortic root.
Connective tissue disorder history: No known personal or family history of connective tissue disorders.
Review of symptoms: Usual state of health with no chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, fatigue, or syncope.
Electrocardiogram: Sinus arrhythmia, otherwise within normal limits and unchanged from prior electrocardiograms.
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Bicuspid aortic valve and enlargement of the aortic root and ascending aorta, with suprasternal notch findings concerning an intimal flap in the ascending aorta just proximal to the branching of the head and neck vessels.
Chest computed tomography: Concerning for a flap extending from the level of the anterior aortic cusp distally for 2.7 cm.
Repeat electrocardiogram: Normal sinus rhythm with left axis deviation.
Cardiovascular magnetic resonance: The right atrial appendage was unusually displaced, coursing leftward and anterior to the aorta.
cases.final_diagnosis: left juxtaposition of the right atrial appendage

cases.case_summary: A 69-year-old man presented with fever and chills one week after hospital discharge.
cases.full_text:
A 69-year-old man presented with fever and chills one week after hospital discharge.
Prior blood cultures: Positive for Haemophilus influenza
Preceding antibiotic course: Two-week course of cefuroxime for Haemophilus influenza bacteremia completed, with discharge one week before this presentation
Prior transthoracic echocardiogram: Ejection fraction 55%, mild aortic stenosis, and moderate aortic insufficiency
Vital signs: Temperature 101 °F, heart rate 127 bpm, blood pressure 67/39 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 96% on room air
Chest pain: Achy, non-radiating, non-reproducible chest pain
Cardiac auscultation: Grade 3 systolic ejection murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border without radiation to the carotids
Admission blood cultures: Positive for beta-lactamase negative H. influenzae serotype F
Transesophageal echocardiogram: Severe aortic insufficiency, valvular destruction, and an aortic valve mass

cases.case_summary: A 13-year-and-11-month-old girl was referred for orthodontic treatment because chewing was inefficient and her smile looked older than her age, with no teeth visible.
cases.full_text:
A 13-year-and-11-month-old girl was referred for orthodontic treatment because chewing was inefficient and her smile looked older than her age, with no teeth visible.
Fracture history: Multiple recurrent fractures, especially of the left midshaft tibia, treated conservatively; the last occurred 6 months earlier after a fall while playing sports.
Standing height and weight: Standing height 138 cm and weight 58 kg.
Facial examination: Euryprosopic face with a deficient midface; upper incisors not visible at rest or on smiling.
Hand examination: Broad hands with short, spoon-shaped phalanges and dystrophic nails.
Eye examination: Brown-black irises with normal-appearing sclera.
Skull radiograph: Frontal bossing, marked suture diastasis, a patent anterior fontanelle, and wormian bodies.
Panoramic radiograph of the mandible: Thin, narrow mandibular body, obtuse gonial angle, and elongated condylar neck.
Serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and complete blood count: Serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase were normal. The blood count showed anisocytosis and hypochromic, microcytic red blood cells, reported as iron deficiency.

cases.case_summary: A 15-year-old boy suddenly developed respiratory distress with paradoxical chest movements while being shifted to the postoperative ward after vitreoretinal surgery under general anesthesia.
cases.full_text:
A 15-year-old boy suddenly developed respiratory distress with paradoxical chest movements while being shifted to the postoperative ward after vitreoretinal surgery under general anesthesia.
Preoperative blood investigations and chest x-ray: Within normal limits
Preoperative anesthetic assessment and intubation: American Society of Anesthesiologists grade I with uncomplicated grade I intubation
Extubation: Uneventful, with an adequate recovery
Respiratory pattern: Sudden brief laryngospasm and respiratory distress with paradoxical chest movements
Oxygen saturation and skin color: SpO2 suddenly dropped to 40%, and the skin became dusky
Ability to breathe: Unable to breathe
Mask ventilation with 100% oxygen: Attempted but not possible, and he desaturated further
Airway secretions and chest auscultation: While fully conscious and responding to commands, pink, frothy sputum appeared suddenly and bilateral crepitations were present

cases.case_summary: A 51-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of progressive weakness in the right leg and dysesthesia in both legs.
cases.full_text:
A 51-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of progressive weakness in the right leg and dysesthesia in both legs.
Symptom history: 2-year history of progressive muscle weakness in the right lower extremity and dysesthesia in both lower extremities
Sensory examination: Severe loss of all sensory modalities below the L1 dermatomes
Motor examination: Monoparesis of the right lower limb, with Manual Muscle Testing grade 1/5 in tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, gastrocnemius, and flexor hallucis longus
Deep tendon reflexes: Hyperactive in both lower limbs
Bladder and bowel function: Slight bladder and rectal disturbance, with constipation and inability to urinate
Sagittal T2-weighted spinal MRI: Cord expansion and hyperintense signal from the Th7 to Th12 vertebral level, surrounding both anterior and posterior aspects of the cord
Sagittal T1-weighted MRI and gadolinium enhancement: Isointense mass lesion without clear demarcation from the spinal cord, with a small enhanced portion after gadolinium
Histopathology: Cells with fine processes and round-to-ovoid nuclei arranged in clusters in a microcystic background; no ependymal rosettes; no anaplasia, necrosis, or increased mitoses; MIB-I labeling index 0.1%

cases.case_summary: A 71-year-old woman presented with ulcerated tumors on her face that had increased in number and size over the past 5 months.
cases.full_text:
A 71-year-old woman presented with ulcerated tumors on her face that had increased in number and size over the past 5 months.
Medical history: Rheumatoid arthritis concomitant with polymyositis for 17 years
Methotrexate history: Methotrexate 10 mg/week for 17 years since the onset of rheumatoid arthritis
Tofacitinib and prednisolone history: Tofacitinib 5 mg/day was added 3 years earlier and systemic prednisolone, started at 30 mg/day and taken for 15 years, was stopped
Presenting symptom: Severe pruritus
Cutaneous examination: Partially ulcerated and crusted tumors 2–5 cm in diameter on the forehead, left cheek, philtrum, and chin
Skin biopsy histology: Diffuse proliferation of lymphocytes with large nuclei, including Hodgkin-like cells, in the dermis and subcutaneous adipose tissue
Immunohistochemistry and EBER in situ hybridization: Positive staining for CD20, CD79a, and CD30, and positive Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA in situ hybridization
Ki-67 immunostaining: Ki-67 staining in 85% of lymphocytes

cases.case_summary: An 11-year-old boy was admitted with a mass in the oral cavity and difficulty chewing and swallowing solid foods for the past 3 years.
cases.full_text:
An 11-year-old boy was admitted with a mass in the oral cavity and difficulty chewing and swallowing solid foods for the past 3 years.
Prior oral or neck surgery or trauma: No previous surgery or trauma to the oral cavity or neck
Dyspnea and pain: No dyspnea or pain
Oral cavity examination: 40 × 35 mm sublingual mass with normal covering mucosa, displacing the tongue superiorly and posteriorly
Neck examination: Firm submental swelling extending down to the thyroid notch
Magnetic resonance imaging: 40 × 35 mm well-circumscribed non-enhancing cystic mass extending from the sublingual area to the thyroid notch, with homogenous content
Thyroid scintigraphy: Normal
Histological examination: Acidophilic stratum corneum and basophilic dot-like staining of the stratum granulosum

cases.case_summary: A 56-year-old Chinese woman had progressive cognitive decline and dizziness for one month. She could not remember recent events and sometimes could not find her way home. A week later she developed stereotyped visual hallucinations of somebody jumping, singing, dancing, or talking with her; they lasted several minutes, occurred dozens of times a day, and frightened her. Her family then brought her to the hospital.
cases.full_text:
A 56-year-old Chinese woman had progressive cognitive decline and dizziness for one month. She could not remember recent events and sometimes could not find her way home. A week later she developed stereotyped visual hallucinations of somebody jumping, singing, dancing, or talking with her; they lasted several minutes, occurred dozens of times a day, and frightened her. Her family then brought her to the hospital.
Recent memory and wayfinding: She was unable to remember recent events and was occasionally unable to find her way home.
Visual hallucinations: Stereotyped complex hallucinations of somebody jumping, singing, dancing, or talking with her, lasting several minutes and occurring dozens of times each day.
Abnormal movements: Focal myoclonic jerks developed gradually after admission.
Mini-Mental State Examination: Score 19/30, with trouble recalling words and locating.
Electroencephalogram: The recording was dominated by generalized periodic synchronous discharges every 0.5 to 1.0 seconds.
Cerebrospinal fluid: Protein and cell values were normal, and 14-3-3 brain protein was negative.
Intravenous valproate and diazepam: After intravenous valproate 1200 mg/24 h and diazepam 20 mg, there was no clinical improvement and the periodic discharges did not disappear.
Motor findings two weeks later: An akinetic-rigid syndrome was present, and the periodic discharges persisted.

cases.case_summary: A 27-year-old woman reported a hard swelling in the posterior mandible, first noticed about 2 years earlier, with an insidious onset and gradual enlargement.
cases.full_text:
A 27-year-old woman reported a hard swelling in the posterior mandible, first noticed about 2 years earlier, with an insidious onset and gradual enlargement.
History of the swelling: First noticed about 2 years earlier, insidious in onset, and gradually increased to the present size
Associated symptoms: No pain, discharge, fever, paresthesia, or difficulty in mastication
Prior trauma or infection: No history of trauma or infection in the region
Physical examination: Solitary, nonpulsatile, nontender, approximately 1.5 cm bony-hard mass palpated at the right mandibular angle
Fixation and overlying skin: Fixed to the underlying bone; overlying skin normal in color and not attached to the mass
Computed tomography: Well-circumscribed hyperdense image with a lobulated surface at the right angle of the mandible
Three-dimensional CT reconstruction: Pedunculated homogeneous bony mass attached to the buccal cortex at the right mandibular angle
Histopathologic examination: Mature compact bone with haversian canals, lacunae containing osteocytes, resting lines, and lamellae

cases.case_summary: A man was readmitted to the emergency department with shortness of breath. Over the previous two weeks he had increasing fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, weight loss, and a dry cough.
cases.full_text:
A man was readmitted to the emergency department with shortness of breath. Over the previous two weeks he had increasing fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, weight loss, and a dry cough.
QuantiFERON assay: Positive; previously negative at the initial diagnosis
High-resolution computed tomography of the chest: No evidence of active lung disease
Temperature: 38°C
Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 5.2 g/dL, white blood cell count 0.3 × 10^3/μL, and platelet count 26 × 10^3/μL
Chest radiography: Faint patchy and linear opacities in the left middle and lower lung fields, and a right-sided pleural effusion
Computed tomography pulmonary angiogram: Right lower pleural effusion with a thick, nodular-enhancing pleural wall, and lung parenchymal changes
Bone marrow biopsy and aspiration: Hypocellular bone marrow with decreased trilineage hematopoiesis, increased histiocytes, and multiple granulomas, with no evidence of Burkitt's lymphoma involvement
Acid-fast bacilli smear and tuberculosis PCR: Positive; rifampicin sensitive

cases.case_summary: A 63-year-old man presented with about one month of right hip pain that had worsened despite painkillers.
cases.full_text:
A 63-year-old man presented with about one month of right hip pain that had worsened despite painkillers.
Childhood lower-limb history: The right ankle was almost rigid after childhood poliomyelitis, with no other apparent functional disorders.
Right hip examination: No marked swelling or local warmth; walking was difficult because of severe pain.
Plain radiographs: Narrowing of the joint space.
MRI of the hip: Mixture of fat and edema in the gluteus medius, slight bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone, and joint effusion.
C-reactive protein and white cell count: C-reactive protein 14.0 mg/dL (reference 0–0.3 mg/dL); white cell count normal.
Open biopsy of the right hip: Apparent purulence from the right hip joint.
Culture of the purulence: Staphylococcus aureus.
Histology: Acute inflammation without atypia.

cases.case_summary: A 33-year-old woman is seen for a routine gynecological check-up. She reports no symptoms and the physical examination shows no findings, but transvaginal ultrasound reveals an adnexal mass.
cases.full_text:
A 33-year-old woman is seen for a routine gynecological check-up. She reports no symptoms and the physical examination shows no findings, but transvaginal ultrasound reveals an adnexal mass.
Past history: Nulliparous; BMI 19.4 kg/m2; no past medical or family history.
Symptom history and physical examination: No symptoms; physical examination had no findings.
MRI of the lower abdomen: Cystic mass of undetermined origin adjacent to the left ovary, 18 × 15 × 20 mm, with high T2 and low T1 signal, a solid nodular element, and enhancement of the cystic wall after intravenous contrast. No abnormal findings in the uterus or right adnexa.
Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler: Multilocular solid mass of undetermined origin adjacent to the left ovary, 20 × 20 × 16 mm, with a solid component of maximum diameter 13 mm and height 7 mm. Uterus and right adnexa were normal in size. The solid component had no Doppler blood supply; one complete septation showed blood supply.
Serum CA-125 and laboratory tests: CA-125 was 13.3 U/ml, and the remaining laboratory tests were normal.
Laparoscopy and rapid biopsy: A mass on the left fallopian tube was excised. Rapid biopsy was negative for malignancy.
Gross examination of the excised mass: Cystic mass measuring 17 × 17 mm, wall thickness 1 mm, with an internal smooth whitish-yellow nodule-like area 10 mm in diameter.
Microscopic examination of the excised mass: Cellular mass with slit-like and tubular spaces covered by cuboidal, cross-striated cells with scant cytoplasm, without atypia or nuclear abnormalities, in a fibrous substrate.
cases.final_diagnosis: adenomatoid tumor of the fallopian tube

cases.case_summary: A 41-year-old woman presented with a slowly growing lump on the anterior side of the left upper arm that had been present for 3 years.
cases.full_text:
A 41-year-old woman presented with a slowly growing lump on the anterior side of the left upper arm that had been present for 3 years.
Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed about 10 years before presentation.
Physical examination: A 2 cm hard, non-tender lump in the distal left biceps brachii muscle.
Motor, sensory, and range-of-motion examination: No motor or sensory deficits distal to the lesion, and no restriction of arm movement compared with the unaffected side.
Ultrasound of the left upper arm: A 2.0 × 2.0 cm well-defined heteroechogenic lesion with a cystic component in the left biceps brachii muscle.
Intraoperative inspection: A solid, well-circumscribed, encapsulated mass that was easily removed.
Histopathology: The tumour was surrounded by muscle fibres.
Histopathology with hematoxylin and eosin: Small spindle- to stellate-shaped cells with pale indistinct cytoplasm and small hyperchromatic nuclei; mitoses were rare.
Histopathology with periodic acid-Schiff and Van Gieson stains: Hypocellular myxoid tissue containing strands of fibrocollagenous tissue.

cases.case_summary: A 67-year-old man presented to the emergency room with severe dyspnea, intense asthenia, myalgia, and fever of 39 °C, two weeks after receiving immunotherapy.
cases.full_text:
A 67-year-old man presented to the emergency room with severe dyspnea, intense asthenia, myalgia, and fever of 39 °C, two weeks after receiving immunotherapy.
Physical examination: On arrival he was conscious and alert with neurological function preserved, hemodynamically stable, and tachypneic, with oxygen saturation 93% on room air. He was pale, with bruises on both arms, painless hepatomegaly and splenomegaly, and abolished left lung sounds.
Leukocyte count: White blood cells 2.58 k/cumm at presentation.
Hemoglobin: Hemoglobin 7.1 g/dL at presentation.
Platelet count: Platelets 25 k/cumm at presentation.
Ferritin: Ferritin 7035 ng/dL.
Interleukin-6, CD25, and angiotensin-converting enzyme: IL-6 19.4 pg/mL and CD25 6516 U/m, with normal angiotensin-converting enzyme.
Viral serologies: Negative for HSV1-2, CMV, EBV, HIV, HBV, HCV, and HLTV-1.
Bone marrow biopsy: Reactive hypercellularity, hemophagocytosis, and dysplastic signs in megakaryocytic and erythroid reactive lines.

cases.case_summary: A 19-year-old girl presented with three seizure-like episodes during sleep over the past 3 months.
cases.full_text:
A 19-year-old girl presented with three seizure-like episodes during sleep over the past 3 months.
Morning event while asleep: Myoclonic jerks, screaming, acute confusion, psychomotor agitation, and irrelevant talk lasting three days.
History of fever, headache, vomiting, or focal deficits: No history suggestive of fever, headache, vomiting, or focal neurological deficits during this period.
Mental status examination: Restless, disoriented, producing an abnormal clicking sound, and not obeying verbal commands.
Electroencephalography: Normal study.
Brain MRI: Plain and contrast study reported as normal.
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Normal cell count, protein, and glucose levels.
Serum anti-TPO antibody and thyroid status: Anti-TPO antibodies 1261.4 U/mL (normal < 60), with euthyroid status.
Voltage-gated potassium channel antibodies: Negative.

cases.case_summary: A 56-year-old woman had progressively worsening generalised body pain and weakness for 7 years, since the age of 48, with a constantly blocked nose and occasional moderate epistaxis.
cases.full_text:
A 56-year-old woman had progressively worsening generalised body pain and weakness for 7 years, since the age of 48, with a constantly blocked nose and occasional moderate epistaxis.
Mobility: Numerous falls, and she was eventually wheelchair bound because of incapacitating pain.
Pelvic and rib radiographs: Diffuse loss of bone mineral, bilateral comminuted proximal femoral fractures with cranially displaced subcapital and transverse subtrochanteric fractures, bilateral inferior and superior pubic rami fractures, and a right posterior 10th rib fracture.
Hand radiographs: Cortical thinning and prominent trabeculae, bilateral metacarpal and phalangeal fractures, and dorsal angulation of the proximal phalanx fractures. No acro-osteolysis and no subperiosteal resorption.
Serum phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone: Inorganic phosphate 0.57 mmol/L (reference 0.78–1.42), alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (reference 42–98), and parathyroid hormone 5.1 pmol/L (reference 1.5–7.6).
Urine phosphate excretion and related laboratory tests: Fractional excretion of phosphate 56% with decreased tubular reabsorption of phosphate. Serum calcium was normal. Urine calcium, bicarbonate, uric acid, protein and glucose were negative.
Whole-body gallium-68 DOTANOC PET-CT: A right-sided sinonasal mass showed intense heterogeneous DOTANOC uptake. Some soft tissue in the lateral nasal passage and nasopharynx was photopaenic. This corresponded to a soft-tissue mass in the right ethmoid sinuses and nasal cavity extending posteriorly into the oro-nasopharynx.
Sinonasal CT: Regions of internal soft-tissue hyperdensity without internal osseous or mineralised matrix.
Tumour histology and immunohistochemistry: Spindle cells in short fascicles with areas of higher and lower cellularity, gritty calcifications, perivascular hyalinisation, and spindle cells condensed around vessels. No pleomorphism, mitotic activity or necrosis. Tumour cells were immunoreactive for SATB2, CD56, ERG and somatostatin receptor 2A.

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old man was referred to an otolaryngology clinic with left nasal obstruction and foul-smelling discharge for five years.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old man was referred to an otolaryngology clinic with left nasal obstruction and foul-smelling discharge for five years.
Nasal symptom course: Left nasal obstruction and foul-smelling discharge for five years, progressively noticed and disruptive over the last 3 years.
Prior medical treatment: Multiple courses of antibiotics and nasal steroids with no benefit.
Nasal foreign-body history: No history of a foreign body introduced into the nasal cavity.
Head trauma history: Head trauma after a car accident in childhood in a sandy area.
Anterior rhinoscopy: Irregular hard material with crustations and thick secretions, stuck between a septal spur and the inferior turbinate in the left anterior nasal cavity.
In-clinic removal attempt: Attempts at removal in clinic failed and caused epistaxis.
Plain X-ray and CT scan: Dense irregular material in the left nasal cavity occupying the floor, without extension outside the nasal cavity.

cases.case_summary: A 57-year-old man is referred from a neighboring community hospital with hypotension and bilateral calf pain.
cases.full_text:
A 57-year-old man is referred from a neighboring community hospital with hypotension and bilateral calf pain.
Recent symptom history: Progressive bilateral leg swelling and pain over the last week, with significant nausea and weakness, then rapid worsening of bilateral calf pain and swelling over the two days before presentation to the worst pain of his life.
Blood pressure: 150/99 in the emergency department; 68/40 at the community hospital before a 2 L normal saline bolus.
Lower-leg examination: Bilateral swollen, rock-hard, tender calves, with limited ankle range of motion and severe pain on plantar flexion and dorsiflexion.
Initial blood work: Hemoglobin 210 g/L, white blood cell count 27.3 × 10^9/L, albumin 26 g/L, and creatinine 135 umol/L.
Compartment pressure measurement: 110 mmHg.
CT angiogram of the lower limbs: Marked narrowing of the distal arteries and veins, without occlusive pathology.
Serum immunofixation: Monoclonal IgG band.
JAK-2 mutation and complement testing: JAK-2 mutation negative; C3 and C4 complement levels normal.

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old man presented on 8 January 2023 with increasing hemiparesis and difficulty speaking. He did not have a fever, chest pain, or dyspnea.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old man presented on 8 January 2023 with increasing hemiparesis and difficulty speaking. He did not have a fever, chest pain, or dyspnea.
Earlier brain CT and pulmonary artery imaging: Right hemiparesis with an acute cerebral infarction on CT. Partial occlusion of distal branches of the right pulmonary artery, without deep vein thrombosis.
Physical examination: Pulse 82 beats per minute, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, mild jaundice, a grade 3 systolic murmur loudest at the apex, and hepatomegaly. Motor dysphasia and hemiparesis graded 3/5. No retinal Roth spots, splinter or conjunctival hemorrhages, Osler nodules, or Janeway lesions.
Transthoracic echocardiography: A 10.7 × 13.8 mm homogenous, slightly hypoechoic mass was attached at the right and non-coronary cusps on the left ventricular outflow side, with restrictive motion and mild aortic regurgitation. A 11 × 4.4 mm mass was attached to the atrial side of the posterior mitral leaflet, with mild mitral regurgitation. A mobile right ventricular lesion measured 43 × 11 mm and had similar echogenicity.
Cardiac multi-slice computed tomography: Homogeneous hypointense lesions on all three aortic valve leaflets, measuring 7 × 13 mm, 4 × 15 mm, and 4 × 6 mm, without contrast enhancement and with little motion. The coronary arteries were normal.
Blood cultures and blood PCR: Three blood-culture sets taken within 24 hours before antibiotics showed no bacterial or fungal growth. PCR did not detect Coxiella burnetti, Aggregatibacter, Cardiobacterium, Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus, Streptococcus suis, Streptococcus pneumonia, other streptococci, E. coli, Klebsiella pneumonia, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, or Aspergillus.
Coagulation studies and autoantibody testing: Protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III were within normal limits. D-dimer was > 7.65 mg/L FEU (reference < 0.5), PT was 21.8 s, and APTT was 42.5 s. Anti-double-stranded DNA and ANA antibodies were negative.
Serum tumor marker concentrations: AFP 2.8 ng/mL (reference < 7.0), CA 19-9 1000 U/mL (reference < 27), CA 12-5 1679 U/mL (reference < 35), and CEA 1000.0 ng/mL (reference < 4.3).
Fine-needle aspiration of the liver mass: Cytology from the liver mass showed carcinoma, without features specific enough to determine the tissue of origin.

cases.case_summary: A 10-year-old boy presented to the outpatient department with a four-month history of progressive left-sided nasal obstruction and intermittent epistaxis.
cases.full_text:
A 10-year-old boy presented to the outpatient department with a four-month history of progressive left-sided nasal obstruction and intermittent epistaxis.
Past medical history: No other health problems.
Coagulation status: Normal.
Anterior rhinoscopy: Fragile, lobular, red-grayish, smooth, polypoidal mass arising anteroinferior to the left inferior turbinate and filling the vestibule.
Posterior rhinoscopy: Normal appearance.
CT of the nose and paranasal sinuses: Soft tissue opacity filling the vestibule of the left nasal cavity, without sinus invasion or bony destruction.
Postcontrast CT: Intense enhancement of the soft tissue.
Gross examination of the excised mass: Lobular, smooth, and red-grayish, about 12 mm long, with a diameter up to 8 mm.
Histopathology (hematoxylin-eosin): Metaplastic squamous epithelium with respiratory epithelium remnants on the surface; beneath it, many irregular blood vessels ranging from capillaries and sinusoids to large vessels, lined by one layer of flat endothelial cells in a fibrous stroma; proliferative fibrosis at sites of repetitive haemorrhage.

cases.case_summary: He was hospitalized for extensive fluid retention in the abdomen and lower extremities and dyspnea, after gaining 15 pounds over the past two weeks.
cases.full_text:
He was hospitalized for extensive fluid retention in the abdomen and lower extremities and dyspnea, after gaining 15 pounds over the past two weeks.
Past medical history: 50-year-old man of Indian ancestry, diagnosed with multiple myeloma three years earlier, whose only other chronic medical issue was mild hypertension.
Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging: Diffuse bone marrow replacement throughout the pelvis and proximal femora, with only small areas of residual fatty marrow in the greater trochanters and femoral heads bilaterally.
Physical examination: Afebrile, heart rate 100 beats/minute, blood pressure 97/50 mmHg, oxygen saturation 96% on 3 liters/minute nasal oxygen, bilateral basilar crackles, jugular venous distension to 12 cm, 2/6 systolic flow murmur at the left upper sternal border, abdominal distension with shifting dullness, liver edge 4 cm below the right costal margin, warm extremities, 3+ bilateral lower extremity edema, and significant scrotal edema.
Admission laboratory studies: Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dl, platelet count 10,000 per microliter, blood urea nitrogen 55 mg/dl, creatinine 1.0 mg/dl, albumin 3.6 g/dl, and calcium 13 mg/dl.
Electrocardiogram: Sinus tachycardia with normal voltage and diffuse T wave flattening.
Echocardiogram: Hyperdynamic left ventricle with normal wall thickness, no regional wall motion abnormalities, no valvular abnormalities, and normal diastolic function.
Cardiac catheterization: Case 1 measurements: heart rate 119 per minute, right atrial pressure 18 mm Hg, right ventricle 58/3 mm Hg with end-diastolic pressure 22 mm Hg, pulmonary artery 49/15 mm Hg with oxygen saturation 84%, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure 32 mm Hg, left ventricle 86/11 mm Hg with end-diastolic pressure 24 mm Hg, aortic pressure 74/49 mm Hg with oxygen saturation 96%, cardiac output 15.17 L/min, systemic vascular resistance 227 dynes-sec-cm-5, and pulmonary vascular resistance 11 dynes-sec-cm-5. Listed normal values include cardiac output 4–8 L/min and systemic vascular resistance 770–1500 dynes-sec-cm-5.
Thyroid panel: Unremarkable.

cases.case_summary: A female professional basketball player in her mid-20s presented to the emergency department with a seven-hour history of worsening, sharp abdominal pain.
cases.full_text:
A female professional basketball player in her mid-20s presented to the emergency department with a seven-hour history of worsening, sharp abdominal pain.
Abdominal pain: Seven-hour history of worsening sharp pain, rated 7 out of 10, exacerbated by movement with no alleviating factors, beginning in the epigastric region and migrating to the right lower quadrant.
Nausea and vomiting: Worsening nausea and emesis in the emergency department.
Review of systems: Negative for diarrhea, constipation, fever, chills, dysuria, and vaginal discharge.
Gastrointestinal and surgical history: No personal or family history of gastrointestinal disorders, no prior pregnancies, and no prior abdominal surgery.
Abdominal examination: Nondistended abdomen with normal bowel sounds in all four quadrants; tenderness to light and deep palpation in the right lower quadrant, without guarding, rebound, or tympany.
Comprehensive metabolic panel, complete blood count, and lipase: All within normal limits.
Serum pregnancy test: Negative.
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast: Distended small-bowel loops with wall thickening and enhancement, decompressed bowel loops distally, and fecalization of the small bowel.

cases.case_summary: A 54-year-old man presented to the clinic with a scrotal wall lesion noticed for a few months and progressively increasing in size. He denied testicular pain and urinary symptoms.
cases.full_text:
A 54-year-old man presented to the clinic with a scrotal wall lesion noticed for a few months and progressively increasing in size. He denied testicular pain and urinary symptoms.
Scrotal examination: A firm 3 cm lesion arising from the left scrotal wall with a narrow neck was palpated. The testes and epididymis appeared normal.
Testicular pain and urinary symptoms: He denied testicular pain and urinary symptoms.
Scrotal ultrasound: Well-circumscribed scrotal-wall abnormality of mixed echotexture, about 4 × 2 cm, with an echogenic wall, internal necrotic or turbid components, and vascularity within the solid-appearing elements.
Ultrasound of the testes, epididymis, and scrotal sac: Both testes and the epididymis showed normal size, echotexture, and vascularity. No hydrocele was seen.
Histopathology: The lesion dissected between muscle fibers and was composed of bland spindle to stellate cells in a myxoid stroma, with a few small blood vessels.
Histologic cellularity and vascularity: The lesion was hypocellular and hypovascular and dissected into the muscle fibers.
Immunohistochemistry: Spindle cells were immunoreactive for smooth muscle actin and calponin, with focal estrogen receptor and desmin expression; negative for CD34, S100, cytokeratin AE1/AE3, EMA, STAT6, MDM2, and CDK4. Ki-67 was approximately 5%.

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old man presented with a painless palatal swelling that had gradually enlarged over five years, with snoring, obstructive sleep apnea, dysphagia, and hypernasal speech.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old man presented with a painless palatal swelling that had gradually enlarged over five years, with snoring, obstructive sleep apnea, dysphagia, and hypernasal speech.
Palatal swelling: Painless swelling in the palate that gradually enlarged over the last five years.
Associated complaints: Snoring, obstructive sleep apnea, dysphagia, and hypernasal speech.
Soft palate examination: A firm, immobile, well-circumscribed large submucosal mass in the soft palate, obstructing the nasopharyngeal port.
Neck examination: No palpable lymph nodes in the neck.
Computed tomography: Well-defined enhancing solid mass, 50 × 35 mm, arising from the right posterior soft palate, without infiltration of adjacent fat planes and without apparent bone involvement.
Fine-needle aspiration cytology: Aspirated material composed of round to oval myoepithelial cells with eccentric nuclei and large eosinophilic cytoplasm.
Histopathology of the excised mass: Encapsulated tumor with plasmacytoid cells and homogeneous eosinophilic cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: Tumor cells showed strong, diffuse positivity for S-100 protein, calponin, and smooth muscle actin.

cases.case_summary: A 41-year-old man with episodic arthritis for 10 years is hospitalized for a polyarthritis outbreak with low-grade fever.
cases.full_text:
A 41-year-old man with episodic arthritis for 10 years is hospitalized for a polyarthritis outbreak with low-grade fever.
Arthritis history: Began in the first right metatarsophalangeal joint, then progressively involved other joints. Over the past 5 years, polyarthritis outbreaks affected large and small joints, with low-grade fever and without morning stiffness.
Musculoskeletal examination: Swan-neck deformity of the fingers that was reversible with passive movement. Ankles, knees, and elbows were swollen and warm.
Subcutaneous nodule examination: Painless subcutaneous nodules of fibrous consistency, 0.5 to 1 cm, on the extensor surfaces of the forearms and legs.
Hemoglobin, leukocyte count, and serum uric acid: Hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, white blood cell count 12700 cells/mm3, and uric acid in the upper normal range at 6.7 mg/dL. Glycemia, total cholesterol, creatinine, and hepatic enzymes were normal.
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 62 mm and C-reactive protein 418 mg/L.
Autoantibody testing: Anti-CCP antibodies by ELISA 38 U, with a negative cutoff value of <20 U. Antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, anti-dsDNA, and anti-SSA/Ro antibodies were negative.
Plain radiographs of the hand: Normal, with no evidence of bone erosions.
Subcutaneous nodule biopsy: Uric acid crystals within the nodules.

cases.case_summary: A 64-year-old man presented to the emergency department with right chest pain after a traffic accident.
cases.full_text:
A 64-year-old man presented to the emergency department with right chest pain after a traffic accident.
Past medical history: He denied any other systemic diseases.
Vital signs: Temperature 36.9°C, blood pressure 131/91 mmHg, and heart rate 77 bpm.
Pulse oximetry: Oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Chest examination: Lungs clear bilaterally, trachea midline, no crepitus, substantial right posterolateral chest wall tenderness, and decreased breath sounds.
Abdominal examination: Soft, non-tender, and non-distended, with no palpable masses or organomegaly.
Chest radiography: Right fifth through eighth rib fractures, and findings suspicious for free air under both hemidiaphragms.
Computed tomography of the abdomen: Bowel loops interposed between the liver and the diaphragm.

cases.case_summary: A 94-year-old man developed a bruise-like rash on his forehead without a clear cause, and it progressively enlarged over 4 months.
cases.full_text:
A 94-year-old man developed a bruise-like rash on his forehead without a clear cause, and it progressively enlarged over 4 months.
Forehead rash history: Bruise-like rash on the forehead without a clear cause, appearing and progressively enlarging over 4 months.
Skin examination: Dome-shaped, dark purple, firm forehead mass measuring 8 × 4 cm², plus multiple pale dark infiltrated eruptions on the crown.
Superficial lymph node examination: No superficial lymph nodes were palpable.
Skin biopsy histology: Diffuse proliferation of atypical cells extending from the dermis to the subcutaneous tissue.
Immunohistochemistry: Atypical cells diffusely and strongly positive for CD4, CD56, and CD123, and negative for CD3, CD34, and lysozyme.
CT scan: Thickening of the skin on the back of the head, with no other significant distant lesions, including none in lymph nodes.
Peripheral blood tests: No cytopenia or abnormal cells in the peripheral blood; severe renal dysfunction was present.

cases.case_summary: A 50-year-old man presented to the orthopedic department after tripping on a step and falling onto his left side.
cases.full_text:
A 50-year-old man presented to the orthopedic department after tripping on a step and falling onto his left side.
Medications: Furosemide, captopril, and metformin
Physical examination: Blood pressure 135/80 mmHg, normal pulse rate, no fever, and no symptoms except left clavicular pain
Radiographs: Lytic lesion in the left clavicle and an asymptomatic lytic lesion in the left humeral head
Computed tomography: Multiple osteolytic lesions throughout the skeleton
Whole-body bone scintigraphy: Diffusely increased uptake in the axial and appendicular skeleton, absent urinary activity, prominent calvarian and periarticular uptake, and focal radiotracer accumulation in the left clavicle
Serum calcium: 3.8 mmol/l (corrected range 2.15 to 2.60)
Parathyroid hormone: 1905 pg/ml (normal range 14 to 72)
Serum creatinine: Within normal limits

cases.case_summary: A 39-year-old woman is reevaluated.
cases.full_text:
A 39-year-old woman is reevaluated.
Initial neurological symptoms: At age 29 she presented with vertigo, ataxia, and left-sided weakness.
Initial cerebrospinal fluid and brain MRI: CSF showed oligoclonal bands. MRI showed multiple white matter lesions in the subcortical, periventricular, and deep white matter of both cerebral hemispheres, the genu of the corpus callosum, and the left middle cerebellar peduncle, with some atrophy.
Symptoms at age 35: Frontal lobe symptoms and executive dysfunction, with increased energy, emotional lability, grandiosity, impulsiveness, and reckless spending.
MRI and FDG-PET after age 35: Neuropsychological evaluation showed significant deficits in multiple cognitive domains. MRI showed progressive frontotemporal atrophy, noted over the prior 2 years on closer review. FDG-PET showed hypometabolism in the frontotemporal lobes and cerebellum.
Lumbar puncture at age 37: Monoclonal bands were no longer detected.
Repeat brain MRI and FDG-PET: Interval increase in cerebellar atrophy and increased hypometabolism in the cerebellum. Metabolic activity in the cerebellum was much less than in the frontal lobe.
Neurologic examination: Difficulty with alternating hand movement and motor sequencing, greater on the left than the right, and a gait with short tentative steps and apparent balance weakness.
Cognitive test scores: Five domains were below the stated passing scores: semantic fluency 14 (passing score 16), category switching 6 (passing score 10), digit span forward 5 (passing score 6), digit span backward 3 (passing score 4), and verbal recall 9 (passing score 11). Total score 73.

cases.case_summary: A 64-year-old woman presented with one week of colicky abdominal pain and partial constipation. One day before admission she developed mucoid, bloody stools and could not pass flatus.
cases.full_text:
A 64-year-old woman presented with one week of colicky abdominal pain and partial constipation. One day before admission she developed mucoid, bloody stools and could not pass flatus.
Earlier abdominal symptoms: Unwell for over one year with an intermittent dull ache, mainly in the left hypochondrium and lumbar region, progressing to cramp-like pain after meals, with diffuse bloating, flatulence, and pellet-like stools. Pain eased slightly after passing flatus. During that time there was no hematochezia or felt abdominal swelling; appetite was preserved, with no weight change, no dyspepsia, and no vomiting.
General examination: Moderately dehydrated, not jaundiced, not anemic, and afebrile.
Abdominal examination: Grossly distended, amorphous abdomen without visible peristalsis; a fine midline sub-umbilical scar; generalized mild tenderness without features of peritonitis; tympanitic percussion and reduced bowel sounds.
Digital rectal examination: Largely empty rectum with normal mucosa and no palpable mass; small amount of bloody, mucoid stool.
