Laparotomy findings: Colocolonic intussusception from the middle of the transverse colon into the descending colon, looping through the splenic flexure. No intraperitoneal adhesions. Involved bowel moderately edematous, neither friable nor gangrenous. After reduction, a large polypoid intraluminal mass with a small stalk on the anti-mesenteric border of the distal third of the transverse colon.
Resected polyp: Stalk 1.5 cm, attached about 12 cm proximal to the splenic flexure. The mass measured 9.5 × 7.2 × 6.0 cm, was uniformly soft, and the mucosa had patches of hyperemia, edema, and hemorrhage.
Pathologic examination of the polyp: Polypoid mass, macroscopically fatty and nodular, 9 cm at its widest diameter, with non-specific acute inflammation within lobules of fat.
Microscopy of the resected polyp: Hematoxylin and eosin section shows necrotic and inflamed mucosa; the submucosa contains hemorrhage and mature adipocytes (magnification ×40).

cases.case_summary: A 16-year-old boy, screened on arrival at a juvenile detention facility, reported 4 days of intractable epigastric pain, pleuritic chest pain, and repeated vomiting, along with dysphagia and odynophagia. He denied any past medical history and denied swallowing a foreign body.
cases.full_text:
A 16-year-old boy, screened on arrival at a juvenile detention facility, reported 4 days of intractable epigastric pain, pleuritic chest pain, and repeated vomiting, along with dysphagia and odynophagia. He denied any past medical history and denied swallowing a foreign body.
Additional history: He said he had swallowed a bag before his arrest and would not disclose its contents.
Physical examination: Normotensive and mildly tachycardic, with moderate epigastric pain and an otherwise normal examination.
Electrocardiogram: Diffuse concave ST elevations, hyperacute T waves, and PR depressions.
Laboratory tests: White blood cells 12.5 × 10^9 per liter, erythrocyte sedimentation rate 28 millimeters per hour, C-reactive protein 21.77 milligrams per decilitre, and procalcitonin 11.02 nanograms per milliliter, all elevated; troponin and the remainder of the complete blood count and basic metabolic panel grossly unremarkable.
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast: Pericholecystic fluid, distal esophageal edema and dilation, questionable air in the esophageal wall, and possible hiatal hernia.
Right upper quadrant ultrasound: Gallbladder wall thickening near the fundus of unclear etiology, no gallstones, and otherwise normal.
Esophagram with water-soluble contrast: Filling defect in the distal esophagus.
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A plastic bag whose contents were suspicious for marijuana was found in the distal esophagus and removed; further analysis confirmed marijuana.

cases.case_summary: A 68-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and the right shoulder, with nausea and without vomiting.
cases.full_text:
A 68-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and the right shoulder, with nausea and without vomiting.
Preceding trauma: No preceding trauma
Medications: Aspirin
Abdominal examination: Soft abdomen with right upper quadrant tenderness and no obvious palpable mass
Hemoglobin: 103 g/L, with 144 g/L documented 5 months earlier
Coagulation profile: Normal
Serum lipase: Normal
CT of the abdomen and pelvis: Extensive oedema and induration surrounding the duodenum with complex hyperdense fluid extending to the paracolic gutters and into the pelvis
MRI of the abdomen: T2-hypointense, T1 iso- to hyperintense material surrounding D2/D3 without enhancement

cases.case_summary: An 18-year-old man was referred after the acute onset of painless obstructive jaundice, with nausea, fatigue, loss of appetite, and icterus. He had no fever and no past history of similar complaints.
cases.full_text:
An 18-year-old man was referred after the acute onset of painless obstructive jaundice, with nausea, fatigue, loss of appetite, and icterus. He had no fever and no past history of similar complaints.
Serum liver biochemical tests: AST 214 IU/L (reference 0–40), ALT 314 IU/L (reference 5–45), alkaline phosphatase 2367 IU/L (reference 104–338), total bilirubin 8.1 mg/dL (reference 0.3–1.2), and direct bilirubin 6.0 mg/dL (reference 0–0.4).
Serum IgG4: Serum IgG4 was 40 mg/dL (reference range 4–108 mg/dL).
Contrast-enhanced CT of the gallbladder and bile ducts: A 30 mm infiltrative low-density mass, with mild enhancement in the arterial and delayed phases, involved the gallbladder neck, upper biliary tract, and hilar bile duct, and the intrahepatic bile ducts were dilated.
Contrast-enhanced CT of the pancreas: The pancreas was not enlarged.
Bile duct exfoliative cytology: Inflammatory cells were present without atypia.
Gross examination of the resected specimen: The specimen contained a 4.5-cm mass involving the gallbladder and the hilum of the liver; the liver was depressed by the mass but not invaded.
Histopathology of the gallbladder: Obliterative phlebitis was present, with eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltration and some xanthogranulomatous inflammation. There were no histologic signs of malignancy, but storiform fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration were present.
IgG4 immunohistochemical staining: The IgG4/plasma cell ratio was 10–40%, with many IgG4-positive plasma cells and a maximum density of 50 per high-power field.

cases.case_summary: A 14-year-old patient was referred to a dentist with mild, numb pain on the right side of her face.
cases.full_text:
A 14-year-old patient was referred to a dentist with mild, numb pain on the right side of her face.
Trauma history: Fall from a height in childhood
Past medical history: No history of a medical condition
Orthopantomography: Extensive unilocular radiolucency from the roots of the right first mandibular premolar to the second molar and ramus, overall length 65 mm
Cone beam computed tomography: Slight expansion and thinning of the buccal cortex with extension beyond the roots; no root resorption or displacement
Pulp vitality test: The teeth were vital
Aspiration: Bloody fluid
Surgical exploration: Blood-containing cavity without an epithelial lining

draft.opening_quote: The infant was referred to our tertiary care Department of Neonatology at 5 days of life for further evaluations. On physical examination, the newborn was in good general conditions. Axial hypotonia and poor head control were evident, as well as poor sucking (Fig. 1 ). The most feature was a peculiar senile appearance (Fig. 2 ).
draft.diagnosis_quote: the first case described in our paper is the only clinical report of an LDS clinically suspected and a molecularly confirmed within the first month of life.

encounter.cutoff: trio whole-exome sequencing

findings.name: Birth history
findings.result: Male third-born infant of non-consanguineous parents with an unremarkable family history and healthy siblings, born vaginally at 38 weeks + 1 day after a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy.
findings.quote: A male, naturally conceived, third-born child of a non-consanguineous couple with un unremarkable family history and healthy brothers and sisters, was born in a secondary-care hospital by vaginal delivery at 38 + 1 weeks of gestation after a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy.

findings.name: Apgar scores and birth measurements
findings.result: Apgar scores 9 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, attributed to persistent hypotonia. Weight 2560 g (10th percentile), length 49 cm (25th–50th percentile), head circumference 35 cm (50th–75th percentile).
findings.quote: At birth, the patient Apgar score was 9 and 9 at respectively 1 and 5 minutes of life, due to persistence of hypotonia. The newborn’s weight was 2560 g (10° percentile), his length was 49 cm (25–50° percentile), and his head circumference was 35 cm (50–75° percentile).

findings.name: First neonatal examination
findings.result: Axial hypotonia, joint hypermobility, right congenital genu recurvatum that resolved within 12 hours, arachnodactyly, and finger joint contractures. Hearing, pulse-oximetry, and inborn-error-of-metabolism screens were normal.
findings.quote: The first neonatal visit confirmed the axial hypotonia, the joint hypermobility, the right congenital genu recurvatum (which had a spontaneous resolution within 12 hours), the arachnodactyly and the fingers joint contractures. All the newborn’s screening tests (hearing, pulse oximetry, and inborn error of metabolism screening) were normal.

findings.name: Facial examination
findings.result: Hypertelorism, down-slanting palpebral fissures, ocular exotropia, arched nose with a bulbous nasal tip, high-vaulted palate, short philtrum, down-turned mouth with a thin upper lip, micrognathia, and low-set ears with evident lobes. No cleft palate.
findings.quote: Several facial dysmorphisms were noticed, including hypertelorism, down-slanting palpebral fissures, ocular exotropia, arched nose with a bulbous nasal tip, high-vaulted palate, short philtrum, down-turned mouth with thin upper lip, micrognathia, and low set ears with evident lobes. Cleft palate was not present.

findings.name: Skin and limb examination
findings.result: Lax, translucent skin; arachnodactyly; contracted finger joints; adduction deformity of the right thumb; clinodactyly and ulnar deviation of all fingers; camptodactyly of the feet with a tendency of the toes to flex; dystrophic nails. No pterygia.
findings.quote: Skin appeared lax and translucent (Fig. 3 ). Furthermore, the patient showed arachnodactyly, contracted finger joints, adduction deformity of the right thumb, clinodactyly and ulnar deviation of all hand fingers. Camptodactyly of the feet was also noticed with a tendency of toes flexion. Nails appeared dystrophic. No pterygia were noticed.

findings.name: Echocardiography
findings.result: Aortic root at the sinus measured 13 mm (Z score +3) without aortic insufficiency; the remaining aortic segments were within limits. Patent foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus with a hemodynamically nonsignificant left-to-right shunt.
findings.quote: the echocardiography revealed an aortic root dilatation at the aortic sinus of 13 mm (Z score + 3) without aortic insufficiency. The remaining segments of the aorta appeared within limits. The patient also presented patent foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus, with a hemodynamically not significant left-to-right shunt.

findings.name: Ophthalmic examination and abdominal ultrasound
findings.result: Exotropia was confirmed, with no other ocular abnormalities. Abdominal ultrasound showed no abnormalities.
findings.quote: The ophthalmic evaluation confirmed the exotropia and did not find any other abnormalities, as well as the abdominal ultrasound.

findings.name: Trio whole-exome sequencing
findings.result: Novel heterozygous de novo missense variant c.1378C>G, p.(Arg460Gly) in TGFBR2 (NM_003242.5).
findings.quote: a trio based Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) was performed finding a novel, heterozygote, missense, de novo variant (c.1378C > G, p.(Arg460Gly) in the TGFBR2 (NM_003242.5) gene.

draft.opening: In May 2020, a 45-year-old woman presents with four years of severe generalized itching and skin lesions and with one month of gradual vision loss in both eyes, recurrent fever, and weight loss.
draft.opening_quote: A 45-year-old Bangladeshi woman was complaining (May 2020) of severe generalized itching and skin lesions over different parts of the body (extremities, neck, upper back, chest, oral cavity, and genitalia) for the last four years ( Figure 1(a) ). During the course of illness, she has taken multiple consultations and was prescribed different topical and systemic antifungals along with steroids. She also received a course of dapsone as a suspected case of dermatitis herpetiform, but showed no significant improvement of the condition. Her baseline investigations were inconclusive. She came to us while experiencing a gradual loss of vision of her both eyes for one month. She also had a history of recurrent fever and weight loss for the same duration.
draft.diagnosis_quote: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for HIV came out to be positive.

encounter.start: May 2020
encounter.cutoff: May 2020
encounter.cutoff_quote: The patient's CD4 count was 237 cells/mm.

findings.name: Exposure and family history
findings.result: Husband has a similar skin lesion for a long time and has lived in South Africa for the last 8 years. Other family members are well, with no similar lesions. She denied tuberculosis or contact with smear-positive tuberculosis and had not received a blood transfusion.
findings.quote: On query, she mentioned that her husband is also suffering from a similar skin lesion for a long time and residing in South Africa for the last 08 years. The rest of her family members are in good health; there was no history of similar lesions in her family. She denied any history of tuberculosis or contact with smear-positive tuberculosis patients. She did not receive blood transfusion in the past.

findings.name: General examination
findings.result: Emaciated and moderately anaemic, with normal vital signs and no lymphadenopathy.
findings.quote: She was found emaciated, moderately anaemic, normal vitals, and without any lymphadenopathy.

findings.name: Skin and mucosal examination
findings.result: Multiple excoriated lichenified papules on the extremities, neck, and upper back, with exudation and crusting of some lesions; whitish patches on the tongue and oral cavity; and a nonhealing ulcer on the labia.
findings.quote: On skin survey, she was found to have multiple excoriated lichenified papules over different parts of the body, e.g., extremities ( Figure 1(a) ), neck, and upper back. There were also exudation and crusting in some lesions. There were some whitish patches over her tongue and oral cavity and a nonhealing ulcer present over her labia.

findings.name: Fundoscopy
findings.result: Right eye with disc swelling, haemorrhage, and exudate in the superior and inferior quadrants; left eye with a pale disc and exudates in the superior and inferior retinal quadrants.
findings.quote: Fundoscopy reveals disc swelling, haemorrhage, and exudate present over superior and inferior quadrants of the right eye and a pale disc with exudates in the superior and inferior retinal quadrants of the left eye.

findings.name: HIV ELISA
findings.result: Positive.
findings.quote: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for HIV came out to be positive.

findings.name: Syphilis, viral hepatitis, and HSV serology
findings.result: Serum VDRL, TPHA, HBsAg, HCV antibody, and HSV-1 and HSV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies were negative.
findings.quote: Other investigations including the serum venereal disease research laboratory (VDRL) test, TPHA, serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibody against HCV, and antibodies (IgM + IgG) against HSV 1 and 2 were negative.

findings.name: CD4 count
findings.result: 237 cells/mm.

encounter.start: Referral with a 3-month history of dyspnoea, hacking cough, and distended jugular veins
encounter.cutoff: Histologic and immunophenotypic result of the mediastinal fine-needle aspirate and chest-wall biopsy
encounter.cutoff_quote: Morphological and immunophenotypic findings (Fig. 7b, c, d ) (PanCK, CK20, chromogranin, NSE were also negative) were compatible with the diagnosis of PBL.

findings.name: Earlier blood count, bone marrow biopsy, and JAK2 testing
findings.result: Seven years earlier, a blood count showed polyglobulia. Bone marrow cellularity was 70%, with trilinear expansion, a myelo-erythroid ratio of 5:1, and preserved maturation; megakaryocytes were slightly polymorphic with little clustering. The marrow was considered highly suspicious for an initial phase of polycythemia vera, and he was then treated with oral 1,4-bis (3-bromopropionyl) piperazine 25 mg and hydroxyurea 500 mg. Three years later, JAK2 V617F was found.
findings.quote: Seven years before, a complete blood cell count had revealed polyglobulia. The subsequent bone marrow biopsy showed a cellularity of 70%, with trilinear expansion; the myelo-erythroid ratio was 5:1, with preserved maturation. The proliferative megakaryocytic series were slightly polymorphic, with little tendency to cluster aggregation. The histology was highly suspicious for an initial phase of polycythemia vera (Vasquez disease). After diagnosis, our patient was placed on oral administration of 1,4-bis (3-bromopropionyl) piperazine 25 mg and hydroxyurea 500 mg. Three years later, JAK2 V617F mutation was found.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Facial rash, periorbital and facial edema, distended jugular veins, bilateral disappearance of the supraclavicular fossae, mild ptosis especially on the right, and a hard chest-wall mass over the sixth right rib.
findings.quote: On physical examination, our patient showed facial rash, periorbital and facial edema, distension of the jugular veins, bilateral disappearance of his supraclavicular fossae, mild ptosis especially on the right side, and a chest wall formation, just upon the projection of the sixth right rib, of hard consistency

findings.name: Blood tests
findings.result: Lymphocytes 17.5% and 1.57×10^3/μL; LDH 423 U/L; CRP 1.8 mg/dL; fibrinogen 414 mg/dL; IgA 549 mg/dL; ESR 27 mm; β2-microglobulin 2.6 mg/dL.
findings.quote: Blood test results showed relative (17.5%) and absolute (1.57*10 3 /μL) lymphocytosis; his lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was 423 U/L; C-reactive protein (CRP) 1.8 mg/dL; fibrinogen 414 mg/dl; immunoglobulin A (IgA) 549 mg/dL; erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 27 mm; β 2 -microglobulin was 2.6 mg/dL.

findings.name: Viral testing
findings.result: Negative for HCV, HHV8, and HIV. Positive for HBV, with HBc IgG 627 mIU/mL, and positive for EBV.
findings.quote: Our patient was negative for hepatitis C (HCV), HHV8 and HIV, but positive for hepatitis B (HBV) (HBc IgG: 627 mIU/mL) and EBV.

findings.name: Total-body computed tomography
findings.result: A few days after admission, a polylobed solid anterior-superior mediastinal lesion was iso-hypodense after contrast and measured 9.7 cm transversely, 8 cm craniocaudally, and 5.7 cm anteroposteriorly. It compressed the right jugular vein and the superior vena cava. The chest-wall lesion had the same radiologic characteristics. No lesion was seen in the abdomen or skull.
findings.quote: A total body computed tomography (CT) scan, performed a few days after admission, showed a polylobed solid heteroplasia to the anterior-superior mediastinum, iso-hypodense after contrast, of 9.7 cm in its transverse diameter, 8 cm in its cranio-caudal diameter and 5.7 cm in its antero-posterior diameter. The heteroplasia compressed the right jugular vein and the superior vena cava. The visible chest wall formation showed the same radiological characteristics as the mediastinal one (Fig. 3 ). No lesion was found in our patient’s abdomen or skull.

findings.name: Histologic examination
findings.result: The mediastinal fine-needle aspirate and the chest-wall biopsy showed the same findings: tissue widely occupied by a monomorphic lymphoid proliferation of large cells with evident nucleoli.
findings.quote: Histological examination of the mediastinal FNAB and the chest wall biopsy gave the same results: resected tissue widely occupied by a monomorphic lymphoid proliferation (Fig. 7a ) composed of large-size cells with evident nucleoli

findings.name: Immunophenotyping

findings.name: Additional immunohistochemical stains
findings.result: Pan-cytokeratin, CK20, chromogranin, and NSE were negative.
findings.quote: PanCK, CK20, chromogranin, NSE were also negative

encounter.start: Presentation with progressive, painless decreased vision in the left eye for 2 months
encounter.cutoff: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry of the enucleated eye
encounter.cutoff_quote: These findings were consistent with a choroidal melanocytoma, not a melanoma.

findings.name: Visual acuity
findings.result: Light perception in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye.
findings.quote: Her visual acuity was light perception in the left eye and 20/20 in the right one.

findings.name: Biomicroscopy of the left eye
findings.result: No conjunctival hyperemia, a clear cornea, and no inflammation in the anterior chamber.
findings.quote: Biomicroscopy of the left eye showed no conjunctival hyperemia, a clear cornea, and no inflammation in the anterior chamber.

findings.name: Fundus examination and fluorescein angiography of the left eye
findings.result: Retinal detachment with a large superior brownish mass.
findings.quote: Fundus examination and fluorescein angiography of the left eye showed a retinal detachment (RD) with a large superior brownish mass

findings.name: B-scan ultrasonography of the left eye
findings.result: Large choroidal dome-shaped mass surrounded by subretinal fluid, with neither acoustic hollowing nor calcification.
findings.quote: B-scan ultrasonography of the left eye revealed a large choroidal dome-shaped mass, surrounded by subretinal fluid, with neither acoustic hollowing nor calcification

findings.name: Magnetic resonance imaging of the orbits
findings.result: Intraocular tumor measuring 12 × 11 × 11 mm, with high signal intensity on T1-weighted images, low signal intensity on T2, collar-button extension, and enhancement on T1-weighted images after gadolinium.
findings.quote: MRI of the orbits showed an intraocular tumor measuring 12 × 11 × 11mm, which displayed a high signal intensity on T1-weighted images, low signal intensity on T2, with a collar-button extension, and an enhancement on T1-weighted images after Gadolinium administration.

findings.name: Extraocular extension on orbital imaging
findings.result: Scleral thickening and no evidence of extraocular tumor extension.
findings.quote: There was a scleral thickening and no evidence of extraocular tumor extension

findings.name: Histopathology of the enucleated eye
findings.result: Brownish-black pigmented tumor arising from the choroid, composed of fusiform cells with brownish cytoplasm, elongated nuclei, and small nucleoli, with no signs of necrosis or malignancy.
findings.quote: The histopathological study of the enucleated eye showed a brownish-black pigmented tumor arising from the choroid, composed of fusiform cells with brownish cytoplasm, elongated nuclei, and small nucleoli. No signs of necrosis or malignancy were found

findings.name: Immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Positive cytoplasmic reaction for S-100 protein and HMB-45 monoclonal antibody.
findings.quote: Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a positive cytoplasmic reaction for S-100 protein and HMB-45 monoclonal antibody.

findings.name: Respiratory and limb symptom history
findings.result: Shortness of breath of subacute onset for 4 years and nonprogressive bilateral lower limb swelling for 6 months.

findings.name: Chest CT
findings.result: Reticular nodular opacities in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe, superior segment of the right lower lobe, and left superior lingular lobe; thickening of the right horizontal fissure; no lung masses or cavitary lesions; pretracheal, right paratracheal, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, largest 2 cm at the right hilum.
findings.quote: Multiple reticular nodular opacities in: -Posterior segment of right upper lobe -Superior segment of right lower lobe -Left superior lingular lobe Thickening of the horizontal fissure on the right side No lung masses or cavitatory lesions Pretracheal, right paratracheal, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (largest: 2 cm at right hilum)

findings.name: Contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys
findings.result: Diffuse ill-defined hypodense lesions in both kidneys without arterial-phase enhancement: left mid-pole lesion 3 cm × 4 cm × 5 cm and right lower-pole lesion 3.5 cm × 3.5 cm × 4 cm.

findings.result: Dense lymphoplasmocytic infiltration and storiform fibrosis with tubulointerstitial nephritis; no granulomata.

findings.name: Neurological examination
findings.result: Right-sided hemisensory loss, described as a residual deficit from a previous stroke, and no objective evidence of peripheral neuropathy.
findings.quote: The neurological examination revealed a right-sided hemisensory loss as a residual deficit from the previous stroke, but despite dysesthesia, there was no objective evidence of peripheral neuropathy.

findings.name: Nerve conduction studies
findings.result: Mononeuritis multiplex.
findings.quote: the patient underwent nerve conduction studies and was found to have mononeuritis multiplex.

findings.result: More than 25 cells per high-power field.
findings.quote: IgG4 staining was positive with immunostaining off more than 25 cells per high power field.

draft.opening: A 59-year-old woman presented with visual disturbances of her left eye and hyperemia of both eyes. She was generally in good health and had a painless moon face.
draft.opening_quote: A 59-year-old woman presented with visual disturbances of her left eye and hyperemia of both eyes. She was generally in good health at presentation except for a moon face countenance without pain
draft.diagnosis_quote: she was diagnosed with stage 4, peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

encounter.start: ophthalmic presentation
encounter.cutoff: histopathologic diagnosis
encounter.cutoff_quote: Based on these results, she was diagnosed with stage 4, peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

findings.name: Earlier evaluation of facial swelling
findings.result: Facial swelling had been noted 1 year earlier. A general systemic examination detected no abnormal findings.
findings.quote: She had noted a swelling of her face 1 year earlier, and she had seen an internal medicine doctor at general hospital. However, the general systemic examination had detected no abnormal findings in her body.

findings.name: Evaluation of neck stiffness
findings.result: Stiffness of the right side of the neck developed 3 months earlier. Echography and computed tomography showed bilateral enlargement of the lacrimal glands and extraocular muscles and enlargement of the right parotid gland. Two right parotid biopsies were within normal limits.
findings.quote: Then she developed stiffness on the right side of her neck 3 months earlier and visited the Otolaryngology Department in our hospital. Echography and computed tomography revealed enlargements of the lacrimal glands bilaterally, the EOMs bilaterally, and the parotid gland on the right side. She had biopsies of the parotid gland on the right side twice, and histopathological examinations showed that the specimens were within normal limits.

findings.name: Ophthalmic examination
findings.result: Visual acuity was 20/25 in each eye, and Hertel exophthalmometry was 15 mm in each eye. The left eye had blepharoptosis and hypertropia. Upward gaze was limited in the right eye, and downward and rightward gaze were limited in the left eye. She had no diplopia or eye pain. Slit-lamp examination showed only chemosis and hyperemia of both eyes, and the fundi were normal.
findings.quote: Our ophthalmic examination showed that her visual acuity was 20/25 OU, and Hertel exophthalmometer measurements were 15 mm OU. Blepharoptosis and hypertropia were found in her left eye. Motility examinations revealed a limited upward gaze in the right eye and limited downward and rightward gaze in the left eye. However, she did not have diplopia or eye pain. Slit-lamp examinations detected only the chemosis and hyperemia of both eyes. Her fundi were normal.

findings.name: Contrast magnetic resonance imaging
findings.result: Discrete spindle-shaped enlargement of the bellies of all extraocular muscles in both eyes, without spillover into the orbital fat. The lacrimal and parotid glands were enlarged, and the subcutaneous tissue of the face was hyperplastic.
findings.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging with contrast showed discrete spindle-shaped enlargements of the bellies of all of the EOMs without a spillover into the orbital fat of both eyes ( Figure 1 ). In addition, enlargements of the lacrimal and parotid glands and hyperplasia of the subcutaneous tissue in her face were detected in the MR images.

findings.name: Peripheral blood tests
findings.result: WBC, CRP, serum IL-2, IgG4, and thyroid-related hormones were within normal limits. LDH and ferritin were slightly higher than the standard level. Tests for adult T-cell leukemia and HIV antibodies were negative, and tests for Epstein-Barr virus were positive.
findings.quote: The results of peripheral blood examinations including WBC, CRP, serum IL-2, and IgG4, and thyroid-related hormones were within normal limits. However, the LDH and ferritin values were slightly higher than the standard level. Tests for adult T-cell leukemia and human immunodeficiency virus antibodies were negative, but those for Epstein-Barr virus were positive.

findings.name: Gallium scintigraphy, flow cytometry, bone marrow aspirate and trephine, and lumbar puncture
findings.result: No abnormal findings were detected.
findings.quote: Systemic examinations for lymphoma by gallium scintigraphy, flow cytometry, bone marrow aspirate and trephine, and lumbar puncture detected no abnormal findings.

findings.name: Biopsy of the left inferior rectus and right parotid gland
findings.result: Atypical cells infiltrated the tissues. The cells were positive for CD3, CD5, CD8, and Granzyme B and negative for CD20, CD56, and CD79a.
findings.quote: histopathological examinations of the biopsies of the inferior rectus muscle of her left eye and the parotid gland on the right side showed an infiltration of atypical cells into the tissues. Immunohistochemical stains showed that the cells were positive for CD3, CD5, CD8, and Granzyme B (T-cell markers) and negative for CD20, CD56, and CD79a (B-cell markers)

draft.diagnosis_quote: the trauma could be the possible cause of calvarial tuberculosis in this case.

encounter.start: Neurosurgery outpatient presentation with a 6-month right frontoparietal swelling
encounter.cutoff: Histopathology of surgically sampled bone
encounter.cutoff_quote: Tissue sent for microscopy showed bony tissue fragments with extensive areas of well-formed epithelioid granulomas with central areas of necrosis

findings.name: Prior head injury
findings.result: A fall 1 year and 6 months earlier caused scalp swelling, a bruise, and a depressed skull fracture in the right frontal area at the same site, managed conservatively.
findings.quote: She had a history of a fall accident 1 year and 6 months ago, which resulted in scalp swelling, a bruise, and a depressed skull fracture (DSF) in the right frontal area (the same site as the current swelling), managed conservatively.

findings.name: Scalp and skull examination
findings.result: Fluctuant right frontoparietal swelling measuring 10 × 7 cm with a palpable bone defect; tender, without signs of inflammation or skin color change; multiple palpable bone defects in the right frontal area.
findings.quote: There was fluctuant swelling over the right frontoparietal area measuring 10 × 7 cm with a palpable bone defect. Except for tenderness, there were no signs of inflammation or skin color changes. There were multiple palpable bone defects in the right frontal area.

findings.name: General physical and routine hematologic examination
findings.result: No abnormality on general physical examination or routine hematologic testing.
findings.quote: General physical and routine hematological examination did not reveal any abnormality.

findings.name: Head CT
findings.result: Extensive bony defect involving both the inner and outer tables, with a slightly hyperdense epidural and subgaleal lesion containing mixed hypodense areas and adjacent brain parenchymal hypodensity.
findings.quote: CT scan of the head revealed an extensive bony defect involving both the inner and outer tables, with a slightly hyperdense epidural and subgaleal lesion with mixed hypodense areas plus adjacent brain parenchyma hypodensity

findings.name: Brain MRI
findings.result: Epidural and subgaleal lesion iso- to hyperintense on T1 and T2 with intervening hypointense areas, T2 hyperintensity in the adjacent brain, mass effect on the brain and lateral ventricle with midline shift, and homogeneous enhancement with non-enhancing hypodense areas.
findings.quote: Brain MRI showed T1 iso to hyperintense and T2 iso to hyperintense epidural and subgaleal lesion with intervening hypointense areas [ Fig. 3 , Fig. 4 ]. T2 image also showed hyperintense signal change in the adjacent brain with mass effect on the brain and lateral ventricle with midline shift. The epidural and subgaleal lesion enhanced homogeneously with non-enhancing hypodense areas in between.

findings.name: Operative inspection of the collection
findings.result: Thin, non-offensive whitish material in the subgaleal and epidural spaces, and a soft whitish cheesy epidural collection with a lesion adherent to the dura.
findings.quote: There was a non-offensive thin whitish collection in both the subgaleal and epidural spaces. The epidural space was filled with a soft whitish cheesy collection with underlying granulomatous lesion adherent to the dura.

findings.name: Inspection for subdural extension
findings.result: No extension of the lesion into the subdural space.
findings.quote: There was no extension of the lesion into the subdural spaces.

findings.name: Bone histopathology
findings.result: Bony tissue fragments with extensive well-formed epithelioid granulomas and central areas of necrosis.
findings.quote: Tissue sent for microscopy showed bony tissue fragments with extensive areas of well-formed epithelioid granulomas with central areas of necrosis

findings.name: Anthropometric measurements
findings.result: Height 113 cm (z-score < −3), weight 13 kg (z-score < −3), body mass index 10.23 kg/m2, and mid-arm circumference 9 cm.
findings.quote: His height was 113 cm (z-score < −3), weight 13 kg (z-score < −3), body mass index 10.23 kg/m 2 , and mid-arm circumference 9 cm.

findings.name: Facial examination
findings.result: Triangular face with a broad forehead, deeply set eyes, hypertelorism, prominent ears, a small pointed chin, and a saddle nose with a bulbous tip.
findings.quote: Our patient had peculiar facial features in the form of a triangular face with broad forehead, deeply set eyes, hypertelorism, prominent ears, small pointed chin, and saddle nose with a bulbous tip.

findings.name: Abdominal examination
findings.result: The left hepatic lobe was enlarged. The liver was firm, with an irregular margin and a slightly nodular surface; liver span was 9 cm along the right mid-clavicular line. The spleen was firm and palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin.
findings.quote: Examination of his abdomen revealed enlargement of the left lobe of his liver. His liver was firm in consistency with an irregular margin and slightly nodular surface. His liver span was 9 cm along the right mid-clavicular line and his spleen was palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin and firm in consistency.

findings.name: Eye examination
findings.result: Posterior embryotoxon, iris strands, and increased intraocular pressure.

findings.name: Hepatitis B and C serology
findings.result: Hepatitis B surface antigen negative and anti-hepatitis C virus antibodies negative.
findings.quote: He tested negative for hepatitis-B surface antigen and anti-hepatitis C virus antibodies.

findings.name: Echocardiography
findings.result: Pulmonary hypertension and tricuspid regurgitation.
findings.quote: Two-dimensional echocardiography showed pulmonary hypertension and tricuspid regurgitation.

findings.name: Liver biopsy
findings.result: Ten portal tracts with conspicuous absence of interlobular bile ducts adjacent to hepatocytes, mild portal inflammation, some fibrosis, occasional nodules, and a few feathery hepatocytes without inflammation.

draft.opening: A 32-year-old Asian woman presents for evaluation of an abnormal chest radiograph. She has no symptoms. A well-defined mass around the apex of the heart has enlarged over the past year.
draft.opening_quote: A 32-year-old Asian female visited us for examination of an abnormality on her chest X-ray. There was a well-defined mass lesion around the apex of the heart. The mass had developed and grown within 1 year (Fig. 1 A, B). The tumor size enlarged from 34 to 64 mm in the largest diameter by chest X-ray. The patient was asymptomatic
draft.diagnosis_quote: Finally, the tumor was diagnosed as desmoplastic fibroblastoma.

encounter.start: Presentation for evaluation of a chest radiograph abnormality
encounter.cutoff: Histopathologic diagnosis after resection
encounter.cutoff_quote: Finally, the tumor was diagnosed as desmoplastic fibroblastoma.

findings.name: Chest radiography
findings.result: On radiographs from 2018 and 2019, the largest diameter of the mass increased from 34 mm to 64 mm.
findings.quote: Chest X-ray taken in A 2018 and B 2019. The tumor size enlarged from 34 to 64 mm in the largest diameter

findings.name: Past medical, family, and exposure history
findings.result: Never smoked. Hyperthyroidism had been treated with thiamazole, and she was medication-free on admission. No history of pregnancy or childbirth. No remarkable family history of illness, including cancer. Desk worker with no history of exposure to certain chemicals or asbestos.
findings.quote: had never smoked, and had a history of hyperthyroidism treated with thiamazole. However, she was medication-free on admission to our hospital. She had no history of pregnancy and no history of childbirth. There was no remarkable family history of illness, including cancer. She is a desk worker with no history of exposure to certain chemicals or asbestos.

findings.name: Chest computed tomography
findings.result: Pear-shaped mass, 80 mm in largest diameter, between the pericardium and the left lung; monotonous, with attenuation 23–32 HU; expansive growth without apparent invasion of adjacent organs.
findings.quote: Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed a pear-shaped mass lesion measuring 80 mm in the largest diameter that had developed between the pericardium and the left lung (Fig. 2 ). The lesion was monotonous and had a computed tomography value between 23 and 32 HU. It was growing expansively and did not seem to invade the adjacent organs.

findings.name: Magnetic resonance imaging
findings.result: Low signal on T1-weighted images and low, heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted fat-saturation images.
findings.quote: The lesion showed a low signal on T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and a low and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted fat-saturation imaging

findings.name: Magnetic resonance imaging for intratumoral fat
findings.result: No fat intensity was detected inside the tumor.
findings.quote: There was no fat intensity detected inside the tumor

findings.name: Histologic examination
findings.result: Paucicellular tumor composed of vaguely arranged bundles of wavy collagen fibers, with sparse cellularity and no apparent cytologic atypia. Nonspecific lymphocyte or mononuclear-cell infiltration of varying intensity was present around tumor vessels. The pedicle consisted of longitudinally arranged fibrous bundles connected to the pericardium.
findings.quote: Hematoxylin–eosin staining showed that the paucicellular tumor was composed of vaguely arranged bundles of wavy collagen fibers (Fig. 5 B). The pedicle of the tumor was composed of longitudinally arranged fibrous bundles connected to the pericardium, suggesting its origin (Fig. 5 C). The cellularity was sparse. The tumor cells did not seem to be atypical. Some nonspecific lymphocyte (or mononuclear cell) infiltration could be seen around the tumor vasculature with different intensities.

findings.name: Immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Positive for alpha-smooth muscle actin, desmin, and CD34, with intact INI1. Negative for cytokeratin AE1/AE3, EMA, beta-catenin, S100 protein, D2-40, MDM2, and STAT6. No infiltration by IgG4-positive plasma cells.
findings.quote: Immunohistochemical analysis showed a positive reaction for alpha-smooth muscle actin (αSMA), desmin, and CD34. Integrase interactor 1 (INI1) expression was intact. Staining for cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), epithelial membrane antigen (EMA), β-catenin, S100 protein, D2-40, MDM2, and STAT6 was negative. There was no infiltration of IgG4-positive plasma cells.

findings.name: Ki-67 index and ALK studies
findings.result: Ki-67 labeling index less than 5%. ALK immunohistochemistry was negative, and fluorescence in situ hybridization showed no ALK gene breakage.
findings.quote: The Ki-67 labeling index was less than 5%. Anaplastic leukemia kinase (ALK) staining was negative on immunohistochemistry. Fluorescent in situ hybridization indicated no breakage of the ALK gene.

draft.opening: A 27-year-old man was admitted in April 2018 after an episode in January 2018 of lip and facial swelling, generalized hives, and weakness.
draft.opening_quote: A 27-year-old male patient was admitted to the Department of Allergology, Clinical Immunology and Internal Medicine for the diagnosis of food allergy in April 2018. The patient was not suffering from chronic diseases and was not taking any regular medication. For a duration of 3 years prior to admission, he had reported a runny nose as well as itching of the nose and eyes occurring in spring. The symptoms related to food allergy appeared in January 2018. The patient exercised in the gym, initially undergoing isometric training and then aerobic exercise on a treadmill. After exercise, he ate 2 kiwi ( Actinidia deliciosa) fruits. There was lip swelling within 5 min after eating the fruit, followed by an itchy scalp and a swollen face. Approximately 60 min later, the symptoms worsened: the patient suffered from generalized hives, general weakness and a "rumbling" sensation in ears.
draft.diagnosis_quote: The patient was discharged with the following diagnosis: Exercise-induced anaphylaxis, food-dependent and allergic rhinitis.

encounter.start: April 2018
encounter.cutoff: Discharge at the end of the admission workup
encounter.cutoff_quote: The patient was discharged with the following diagnosis: Exercise-induced anaphylaxis, food-dependent and allergic rhinitis.

findings.name: Circumstances of the January episode
findings.result: Symptoms began in January 2018 after gym exercise (isometric training, then treadmill), when he ate 2 kiwi fruits (Actinidia deliciosa). Lip swelling started within 5 minutes, followed by an itchy scalp and facial swelling. About 60 minutes later he developed generalized hives, weakness, and a rumbling sensation in the ears. Symptoms improved within 25 minutes after antihistamines, but facial swelling lasted 24 hours.
findings.quote: The symptoms related to food allergy appeared in January 2018. The patient exercised in the gym, initially undergoing isometric training and then aerobic exercise on a treadmill. After exercise, he ate 2 kiwi ( Actinidia deliciosa) fruits. There was lip swelling within 5 min after eating the fruit, followed by an itchy scalp and a swollen face. Approximately 60 min later, the symptoms worsened: the patient suffered from generalized hives, general weakness and a "rumbling" sensation in ears. The patient's condition improved within 25 min of consuming antihistamines, but the swelling of the face persisted for 24 h.

findings.name: Earlier kiwi ingestion
findings.result: He had previously eaten kiwi without any symptoms.
findings.quote: The patient had previously eaten kiwi without any issues.

findings.name: Other possible contributors on the day of the reaction
findings.result: He denied excessive stress, alcohol, and NSAID use as factors that could have worsened the reaction. He ate breakfast that day but could not recall the foods.
findings.quote: The patient denied any other contributing factors which potentially could have enhanced an allergic reaction, such as excessive stress, alcohol or NSAID consumption. On the day of allergic reaction he ate a regular breakfast, but cannot remember the specific foods he consumed.

findings.name: Prick-by-prick test with fresh kiwi
findings.result: Positive.
findings.quote: The skin prick by a prick test with fresh kiwi fruit was positive.

findings.name: Skin prick tests with foods
findings.result: Negative for rye flour, wheat flour, barley flour, orange, clementine, banana, potato, pepper, cod, carp, chicken egg, cow's milk, pork, beef, and meat II.
findings.quote: skin prick tests that were negative for rye flour, wheat flour, barley flour, orange, clementine, banana, potato, pepper, cod, carp, chicken egg, cow's milk, pork, beef and meat II.

findings.name: Exercise provocation while fasting
findings.result: After a 10-minute bicycle warm-up reaching a heart rate of 120 bpm at 4 minutes, he exercised on a treadmill for 10 minutes at 80%–90% of maximum heart rate. He had no side effects during or after exercise.
findings.quote: On the first day, the patient attempted to perform an exercise provocation on an empty stomach by warming up on a bicycle ergometer for 10 min at a speed leading to heart rate of 120 bpm after 4 min of exercise. The actual exercise challenge was performed on a treadmill with continuous monitoring of the heart rate at 80%–90% of the maximum heart rate (HR max) for 10 min. The patient completed the trial without displaying any side effects during and after exercise.

findings.name: Kiwi ingestion without exercise
findings.result: He ate 2 ripe, peeled kiwi fruits in incremental doses and had no adverse effects over 24 hours of observation.
findings.quote: On the second day, the patient consumed 2 ripe, peeled kiwi fruits in incremental doses in the monitored room. The patient did not present any adverse effects during the 24-h observation period.

findings.name: Kiwi ingestion followed by exercise
findings.result: He ate one kiwi fruit, was observed for 30 minutes, then exercised. Five minutes after exercise he developed abdominal pain, urticarial lesions on the face, and a dry cough. Examination showed single wheezing over the lung fields, heart rate 80 bpm, and blood pressure 117/82 mmHg.
findings.quote: On the next day, the patient ate a kiwi fruit. Following 30 min of observation, an exercise challenge was performed according to the protocol described above. Five minutes after the exercise, the patient developed abdominal pain, skin lesions in the form of urticarial on the skin of the face and dry cough. A physical examination revealed single wheezing over the lung fields, heart rate of 80 bpm and blood pressure of 117/82 mmHg.

findings.quote: The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lower abdomen reported the presence of a cystic mass of undetermined origin, adjacent to the left ovary; its dimensions were 18 × 15 × 20 mm. findings.quote: The transvaginal ultrasound revealed a multilocular solid mass of undetermined origin situated adjacent to the left ovary. The dimensions of the mass were measured at 20 × 20 × 16 mm. Within the mass, a solid component was identified, with a maximum diameter of 13 mm and height of 7 mm. The dimensions of the uterus were within the normal range, as were those of the right adnexa. The solid component did not exhibit any blood supply in the color Doppler examination. However, it is noteworthy that one of the complete septations within the mass demonstrated evidence of blood supply.

findings.name: Pelvic and rib radiographs
findings.result: Diffuse loss of bone mineral, bilateral comminuted proximal femoral fractures with cranially displaced subcapital and transverse subtrochanteric fractures, bilateral inferior and superior pubic rami fractures, and a right posterior 10th rib fracture.

findings.name: Hand radiographs

findings.name: Serum phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone
findings.result: Inorganic phosphate 0.57 mmol/L (reference 0.78–1.42), alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (reference 42–98), and parathyroid hormone 5.1 pmol/L (reference 1.5–7.6).
findings.quote: Reduced inorganic phosphate levels of 0.57 mmol/L (0.78–1.42); raised alkaline phosphatase levels of 420 U/L (42–98) and normal parathyroid hormone levels of 5.1 pmol/L (1.5–7.6) were seen.

findings.name: Urine phosphate excretion and related laboratory tests
findings.result: Fractional excretion of phosphate 56% with decreased tubular reabsorption of phosphate. Serum calcium was normal. Urine calcium, bicarbonate, uric acid, protein and glucose were negative.
findings.quote: Urine confirmed urine-phosphate losses with a fractional excretion of 56%, as well as a decreased tubular reabsorption of phosphate. Serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) was normal, as was the serum calcium, which ruled out parathyroid pathology. There were no other abnormalities found on urine analysis: urine calcium, bicarbonate, uric acid, protein and glucose were all negative

findings.name: Whole-body gallium-68 DOTANOC PET-CT
findings.result: A right-sided sinonasal mass showed intense heterogeneous DOTANOC uptake. Some soft tissue in the lateral nasal passage and nasopharynx was photopaenic. This corresponded to a soft-tissue mass in the right ethmoid sinuses and nasal cavity extending posteriorly into the oro-nasopharynx.

findings.name: Sinonasal CT

findings.quote: There were regions of internal soft tissue hyperdensity on uncontrasted CT, but no internal osseous or mineralised matrix.

findings.name: Tumour histology and immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Spindle cells in short fascicles with areas of higher and lower cellularity, gritty calcifications, perivascular hyalinisation, and spindle cells condensed around vessels. No pleomorphism, mitotic activity or necrosis. Tumour cells were immunoreactive for SATB2, CD56, ERG and somatostatin receptor 2A.
findings.quote: a proliferation of spindle cells arranged in short fascicles, creating areas of both heightened and reduced cellularity. Prominent gritty calcifications were observed, alongside perivascular hyalinisation and the condensation of spindle cells around vessels resembling those found in haemangiopericytoma. Notably, there were no signs of pleomorphism, mitotic activity or necrosis. Immunoreactivity was observed in tumour cells for SATB2, CD56, ERG, and somatostatin receptor 2A (SSTR 2A)

draft.opening: A 53-year-old man presented on 8 January 2023 with increasing hemiparesis and difficulty speaking. He did not have a fever, chest pain, or dyspnea.
draft.opening_quote: A 53‐year‐old male with a known history of untreated gallbladder stones first presented at another hospital with right hemiparesis secondary to an acute cerebral infarction noted on cerebral computed tomography. On further imaging work‐up, partial occlusion in distal branches of the right pulmonary artery was incidentally found without evidence of deep vein thrombosis. He was discharged with residual hemiparesis on 15 mg of daily rivaroxaban. On 8 January 2023, he presented to Bach Mai Hospital complaining of increasing hemiparesis and difficulty speaking; he did not have a fever, chest pain, or dyspnea.
draft.diagnosis_quote: After multidisciplinary team consultation, the patient was diagnosed with NBTE associated with advanced cholangiocarcinoma with multiple embolic complications.

encounter.start: 8 January 2023
encounter.cutoff: Pulmonary artery CT and abdominal artery ultrasound at the end of the admission workup
encounter.cutoff_quote: A MSCT of the pulmonary artery revealed partial or complete occlusion of several segmental branches and consolidation of the laterobasal segment of the right lower lobe. Ultrasonography of abdominal arteries was unremarkable.

findings.name: Earlier brain CT and pulmonary artery imaging
findings.result: Right hemiparesis with an acute cerebral infarction on CT. Partial occlusion of distal branches of the right pulmonary artery, without deep vein thrombosis.
findings.quote: right hemiparesis secondary to an acute cerebral infarction noted on cerebral computed tomography. On further imaging work‐up, partial occlusion in distal branches of the right pulmonary artery was incidentally found without evidence of deep vein thrombosis.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Pulse 82 beats per minute, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, mild jaundice, a grade 3 systolic murmur loudest at the apex, and hepatomegaly. Motor dysphasia and hemiparesis graded 3/5. No retinal Roth spots, splinter or conjunctival hemorrhages, Osler nodules, or Janeway lesions.
findings.quote: He had a pulse of 82 beats per minute, a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, mild jaundice, a grade 3 systolic murmur best heard over the apex of the heart, and hepatomegaly. He did not have retinal Roth spots, splinter or conjunctival hemorrhages, Osler's nodules, or Janeway's lesions. He had a motor dysphasia and a hemiparesis of 3/5 on the Medical Research Council scale for muscle strength.

findings.name: Transthoracic echocardiography
findings.result: A 10.7 × 13.8 mm homogenous, slightly hypoechoic mass was attached at the right and non-coronary cusps on the left ventricular outflow side, with restrictive motion and mild aortic regurgitation. A 11 × 4.4 mm mass was attached to the atrial side of the posterior mitral leaflet, with mild mitral regurgitation. A mobile right ventricular lesion measured 43 × 11 mm and had similar echogenicity.
findings.quote: Routine transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) revealed an aortic valve vegetation‐like mass, measuring 10.7 × 13.8 mm, with a homogenous, slightly hypoechoic texture; this mass was attached to the edge of the right coronary cusp and non‐coronary cusp on the left ventricle outflow tract side, where it displayed restrictive movements during the cardiac cycle and was associated with mild aortic regurgitation. There was a second vegetation‐like mass attached to the atrial side of the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve, measuring 11 × 4.4 mm. There was a mild mitral regurgitation. A right ventricular mobile lesion, measuring 43 × 11 mm with similar echogenicity, was also seen

findings.name: Cardiac multi-slice computed tomography
findings.result: Homogeneous hypointense lesions on all three aortic valve leaflets, measuring 7 × 13 mm, 4 × 15 mm, and 4 × 6 mm, without contrast enhancement and with little motion. The coronary arteries were normal.
findings.quote: cardiac MSCT revealed hypointense lesions on all 3 aortic valve leaflets, measuring 7 × 13, 4 × 15, and 4 × 6 mm, which had a homogeneous texture, lacked contrast enhancement, and demonstrated little movement during the cardiac cycle (Figure 2E ). The coronary arteries were normal.

findings.name: Blood cultures and blood PCR
findings.result: Three blood-culture sets taken within 24 hours before antibiotics showed no bacterial or fungal growth. PCR did not detect Coxiella burnetti, Aggregatibacter, Cardiobacterium, Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus, Streptococcus suis, Streptococcus pneumonia, other streptococci, E. coli, Klebsiella pneumonia, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, or Aspergillus.
findings.quote: Three sets of blood cultures collected within 24 h before antibiotic initiation were negative for bacterial and fungal growth, and the PCR was negative for the detection of Coxiella burnetti, Aggregatibacter sp., Cardiobacterium sp., Staphylococcus aureus , Enterococcus sp., Streptococcus suis , Streptococcus pneumonia, other Streptococcus sp., E. coli , Klebsiella pneumonia, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Aspergillus.

findings.name: Coagulation studies and autoantibody testing
findings.result: Protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III were within normal limits. D-dimer was > 7.65 mg/L FEU (reference < 0.5), PT was 21.8 s, and APTT was 42.5 s. Anti-double-stranded DNA and ANA antibodies were negative.
findings.quote: The protein C, protein S, and anti–thrombin III results were within the normal limits; D‐dimer levels were > 7.65 mg/L FEU (< 0.5), as were the PT at 21.8 s, and APTT at 42.5 s. Anti‐double‐stranded DNA and ANA antibodies were negative.

findings.name: Serum tumor marker concentrations
findings.result: AFP 2.8 ng/mL (reference < 7.0), CA 19-9 1000 U/mL (reference < 27), CA 12-5 1679 U/mL (reference < 35), and CEA 1000.0 ng/mL (reference < 4.3).
findings.quote: an alpha fetoprotein (AFP) concentration of 2.8 ng/mL (< 7.0), a remarkably high cancer antigen concentration: CA 19–9: 1000 U/mL (< 27), CA 12–5: 1679 U/mL (< 35), and a carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration of 1000.0 ng/mL (< 4.3).

findings.name: Fine-needle aspiration of the liver mass
findings.result: Cytology from the liver mass showed carcinoma, without features specific enough to determine the tissue of origin.
findings.quote: he underwent a fine needle aspiration of the liver mass; histological examination confirmed a carcinoma but lacked specificity determining the tissue origin

findings.name: Past medical history
findings.result: 50-year-old man of Indian ancestry, diagnosed with multiple myeloma three years earlier, whose only other chronic medical issue was mild hypertension.
findings.quote: A 50-year-old man of Indian ancestry who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma three years earlier was evaluated in our hospital. His only other chronic medical issue was mild hypertension.

findings.name: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
findings.result: Diffuse bone marrow replacement throughout the pelvis and proximal femora, with only small areas of residual fatty marrow in the greater trochanters and femoral heads bilaterally.
findings.quote: Diffuse bone marrow replacement throughout the pelvis and proximal femora with only small areas of residual fatty marrow in the greater trochanters and femoral heads bilaterally.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Afebrile, heart rate 100 beats/minute, blood pressure 97/50 mmHg, oxygen saturation 96% on 3 liters/minute nasal oxygen, bilateral basilar crackles, jugular venous distension to 12 cm, 2/6 systolic flow murmur at the left upper sternal border, abdominal distension with shifting dullness, liver edge 4 cm below the right costal margin, warm extremities, 3+ bilateral lower extremity edema, and significant scrotal edema.
findings.quote: On initial examination, he was afebrile with a heart rate of 100 beats/minute and a blood pressure of 97/50 mmHg. His oxygen saturation was 96% while receiving oxygen at 3 liters/minute by nasal cannula. He had crackles at the bases of his lungs bilaterally. His cardiovascular exam was remarkable for 12 cm of jugular venous distension and tachycardia with a 2/6 systolic flow murmur at the left upper sternal border. His abdomen was distended with shifting dullness to percussion and a liver edge 4 cm below the right costal margin. His extremities were warm to touch with 3 + bilateral lower extremity edema as well as significant scrotal edema.

findings.result: Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dl, platelet count 10,000 per microliter, blood urea nitrogen 55 mg/dl, creatinine 1.0 mg/dl, albumin 3.6 g/dl, and calcium 13 mg/dl.

draft.opening_quote: A 54-year-old man with a medical history of hypertension, coronary artery disease requiring previous percutaneous coronary intervention, dyslipidemia, and a history of smoking presented to the clinic with a scrotal wall lesion noticed for a few months, progressively increasing in size. He denied any testicular pain or urinary symptoms.
draft.diagnosis_quote: Based on the morphologic and immunophenotypic characteristics, the diagnosis of scrotal wall myxoma was rendered.

encounter.start: Clinic presentation with a scrotal wall lesion
encounter.cutoff: Histopathologic and immunohistochemical diagnosis of the excised scrotal wall lesion
encounter.cutoff_quote: Based on the morphologic and immunophenotypic characteristics, the diagnosis of scrotal wall myxoma was rendered.

findings.name: Scrotal examination
findings.result: A firm 3 cm lesion arising from the left scrotal wall with a narrow neck was palpated. The testes and epididymis appeared normal.
findings.quote: a firm 3 cm lesion arising from the left scrotal wall with a narrow neck was palpated. The testes and epididymis appeared normal.

findings.name: Testicular pain and urinary symptoms
findings.result: He denied testicular pain and urinary symptoms.
findings.quote: He denied any testicular pain or urinary symptoms.

findings.name: Scrotal ultrasound
findings.result: Well-circumscribed scrotal-wall abnormality of mixed echotexture, about 4 × 2 cm, with an echogenic wall, internal necrotic or turbid components, and vascularity within the solid-appearing elements.
findings.quote: a well-circumscribed abnormality of mixed echotexture at the site of concern in the scrotal wall. It measured around 4 × 2 cm in size. The lesion had an echogenic wall and internal necrotic or turbid components with vascularity noted within the solid-appearing elements.

findings.name: Ultrasound of the testes, epididymis, and scrotal sac
findings.result: Both testes and the epididymis showed normal size, echotexture, and vascularity. No hydrocele was seen.
findings.quote: Both testes and epididymis showed normal size, echotexture, and vascularity. No hydrocele was seen

findings.name: Histopathology
findings.result: The lesion dissected between muscle fibers and was composed of bland spindle to stellate cells in a myxoid stroma, with a few small blood vessels.
findings.quote: a scrotal wall lesion dissecting in between the muscle fibers composed of bland spindle to stellate cells embedded in myxoid stroma. Few associated small blood vessels were noted.

findings.name: Histologic cellularity and vascularity
findings.result: The lesion was hypocellular and hypovascular and dissected into the muscle fibers.
findings.quote: the myxoid lesion is hypocellular and hypovascular, and dissecting into the muscle fibers

findings.name: Immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Spindle cells were immunoreactive for smooth muscle actin and calponin, with focal estrogen receptor and desmin expression; negative for CD34, S100, cytokeratin AE1/AE3, EMA, STAT6, MDM2, and CDK4. Ki-67 was approximately 5%.
findings.quote: the spindle cells were immunoreactive for smooth muscle actin and calponin, with focal expression of estrogen receptor (ER) and desmin. They were negative for CD34, S100, Cytokeratin AE1/AE3, epithelial membrane antigen (EMA), STAT6, MDM2, and CDK4. The Ki-67 proliferation index was approximately 5%

draft.opening: A 64-year-old woman presented with one week of colicky abdominal pain and partial constipation. One day before admission she developed mucoid, bloody stools and could not pass flatus.
draft.opening_quote: A 64-year-old African-Ugandan woman of Bantu ethnicity presented to Mulago National Hospital following referral from a private health facility 80 miles from Kampala, Uganda’s capital. Though the referral was to the local regional referral hospital, her relatives opted for the national referral hospital. She had experienced symptoms of abdominal pain and partial constipation for one week. The pain was characteristically colicky in nature. One day prior to admission, she developed mucoid, bloody stool motions, but had no frank diarrhea or distinctively foul-smelling stool. She was also unable to pass flatus.
draft.diagnosis_quote: It was concluded that this was an infected submucosal lipoma.

encounter.start: Hospital presentation with one week of abdominal pain and partial constipation
encounter.cutoff: Histologic examination of the resected colonic polyp
encounter.cutoff_quote: It was concluded that this was an infected submucosal lipoma.

findings.name: Earlier abdominal symptoms
findings.result: Unwell for over one year with an intermittent dull ache, mainly in the left hypochondrium and lumbar region, progressing to cramp-like pain after meals, with diffuse bloating, flatulence, and pellet-like stools. Pain eased slightly after passing flatus. During that time there was no hematochezia or felt abdominal swelling; appetite was preserved, with no weight change, no dyspepsia, and no vomiting.
findings.quote: She had generally been unwell for over one year, with a dull abdominal ache of insidious onset; the pain was on and off, located mainly in the left hypochondrium and lumbar region. The ache progressed to cramp-like pain, especially after meals. Associated with this was diffuse abdominal bloating and flatulence with pellet-like stool motions. Her pain was slightly relieved by passing flatus. Otherwise, she had neither had hematochezia during that time, nor had she felt any swelling in her abdomen. Her appetite was good and she felt she had neither gained nor lost weight. She had not had dyspeptic symptoms and had not been vomiting.

findings.name: General examination
findings.result: Moderately dehydrated, not jaundiced, not anemic, and afebrile.
findings.quote: She was moderately dehydrated, neither jaundiced nor anemic, and afebrile.

findings.name: Abdominal examination
findings.result: Grossly distended, amorphous abdomen without visible peristalsis; a fine midline sub-umbilical scar; generalized mild tenderness without features of peritonitis; tympanitic percussion and reduced bowel sounds.
findings.quote: Her abdomen was grossly distended, more peripherally, though generally amorphous. There was no visible peristalsis. She had a fine, midline, sub-umbilical scar. Superficially, there was generalized, mild tenderness, though with no characteristic features of peritonitis. This was tympanitic to percussion, and bowel sounds were reduced.

findings.name: Digital rectal examination
findings.result: Largely empty rectum with normal mucosa and no palpable mass; small amount of bloody, mucoid stool.
findings.quote: A digital rectal examination revealed a largely empty rectum with a normal mucosa, and no masses were felt. There were small amounts of bloody, mucoid stool.

findings.name: Laparotomy findings
findings.result: Colocolonic intussusception from the middle of the transverse colon into the descending colon, looping through the splenic flexure. No intraperitoneal adhesions. Involved bowel moderately edematous, neither friable nor gangrenous. After reduction, a large polypoid intraluminal mass with a small stalk on the anti-mesenteric border of the distal third of the transverse colon.
findings.quote: A colocolonic intussusception was identified with the invagination extending from the middle part of the transverse colon to the descending colon, looping through the splenic flexure. No intraperitoneal adhesions were found. The gut involved was moderately edematous, though neither friable nor gangrenous. The intussusceptum was gently ‘milked’ proximally and freed. A large, polypoid, intraluminal mass was palpated (Figure 1 ). It had a small stalk attached to the anti-mesenteric border of the distal third of the transverse colon.

findings.name: Resected polyp
findings.result: Stalk 1.5 cm, attached about 12 cm proximal to the splenic flexure. The mass measured 9.5 × 7.2 × 6.0 cm, was uniformly soft, and the mucosa had patches of hyperemia, edema, and hemorrhage.
findings.quote: Its stalk (1.5cm) was attached approximately 12cm proximal to the splenic flexure. It measured 9.5×7.2×6.0cm, and was uniformly soft. The mucosa had patches of hyperemia, edema and hemorrhage (Figure 2 ).

findings.name: Pathologic examination of the polyp
findings.result: Polypoid mass, macroscopically fatty and nodular, 9 cm at its widest diameter, with non-specific acute inflammation within lobules of fat.
findings.quote: Pathological examination revealed a polypoid mass, macroscopically fatty and nodular in nature. It measured 9cm at its widest diameter (Figure 2 ). Histologically, there was non-specific, acute inflammation within the lobules of fat seen (Figure 3 ).

findings.name: Microscopy of the resected polyp
findings.result: Hematoxylin and eosin section shows necrotic and inflamed mucosa; the submucosa contains hemorrhage and mature adipocytes (magnification ×40).
findings.quote: Hematoxylin and eosin stained section of gut showing necrotic and inflamed mucosa ( A ). The submucosa contains areas of hemorrhage ( B ) and mature adipocytes ( C ) (magnification ×40, objective lens).
